items.design:
## BL-162 — Tile construction ledger: the per-candidate expected-profit chart

### Status of the existing surface (verified 2026-07-30 against the code)

The backlog's original prose — "the construction entry point cannot build" — is **stale and
superseded**. `ui::draw_construction_ledger` (`src/ui/selection_panel.cpp:1265`, declared
`selection_panel.hpp:70`, drawn from `app.cpp:2666`) already works end to end:

- enumerates candidates (`:1323-1332`) — one extraction row per extractable resource actually
  deposited on the tile, then Processing Facility / Port / Launchpad / Inland Logistics Hub, plus
  a separate three-tier road block (`:1398-1475`);
- prints full cost, credits then materials (`:1364-1369`);
- prints a reason-coded validity read from `placement_rules::can_place_in_world` (`:1342`, `:1390`);
- has a Build action that genuinely enqueues via `ui.construction.pending_tile/type/target`
  (`:1375-1380`), drained by `app.cpp:2675-2705` into the real `construct_building`.

`docs/ui/SELECTION.md` is correct. **Nothing above is redesigned or rebuilt.** The one placeholder
is the 56x56 grey box at `:1350-1357` (and its road twin at `:1430-1436`).

### What this item delivers

Replace the placeholder image with a **per-candidate expected-profit read**: every buildable
candidate carries a horizontal magnitude bar, drawn on a **ceiling shared across the whole list**,
so the player can rank the options on this tile at a glance and sorted so the best five are the
five on screen. Two adjacent defects that the chart makes intolerable are fixed in the same pass
(a lying affordability gate; the ledger closing itself on every build).

---

### 1. The prospective estimator (the seam)

`estimate_building_profit` **cannot** be used. It hard-requires an existing `building_component`
(`building_profit.cpp:14-17`) *and* a matching `report.buildings` row (`:20-24`), and its revenue is
`br->output_quantity` — a realised figure, not a model. Both miss on an empty tile.

Add a sibling to `src/world/building_profit.{hpp,cpp}`, returning the **same `building_profit`
struct** so a candidate's numbers read identically to a built building's:

```cpp
/// Expected per-tick unit economics of a building that does NOT yet exist, on `tile_id`.
/// Pure read of `world` + `registry` — no economy_report, no RNG, no caches.
building_profit estimate_prospective_profit(const world& w, const recipe_registry& reg,
                                            entity_id tile_id, building_type type,
                                            resource_type target,
                                            std::uint16_t recipe_id = no_recipe);
```

Model, fixed and explicit:

| Term | Value | Mirrors |
|---|---|---|
| `workforce_assigned` | `0.5f`, or `0.0f` for `port` / `inland_logistics_hub` | `construction.cpp:84-85` |
| `workforce_target` | `100` | `building_component`'s default |
| contention scalar | `1.0f` (no economy_report; assume no labour shortage) | stated in the caption |
| habitability | `body_mean_habitability(w, body)` | `apply_budget` exactly |
| `maintenance`, `wages` | `compute_building_opex(synthetic_bc, reg.economics(type), 1.0f, hab)` | exact budget parity |
| extraction revenue | `base_rate * tc.resource_deposit[target] * wf * (1 - tc.hazard_level) * price(target)` | `economy_system.cpp:71`, `wt_scalar = 1` |
| processing | `batches = base_rate * wf`; revenue `= Σ outputs[r]*batches*price(r)`; `input_cost = Σ inputs[r]*batches*price(r)` | `run_processing` |
| port / launchpad / hub | `revenue = 0`, `input_cost = 0` | they produce nothing |

`price(r)` is the tile's market: `market_for_tile(w, tile_id)` → `price[r] > 0 ? price[r] :
base_price[r]` (the `local_price` shape from `corp_ai.cpp:35`; keep it file-local in
`building_profit.cpp`). `has_data = false` when the tile is missing **or** no market resolves — a
chart of zeros is a lie.

**Deliberately not modelled** (do not "improve" these):
- **Price response.** No supply-shift elasticity; today's prices, flat. `solve_workforce_target`'s
  `wf_target_price` is not reused — a half-modelled elasticity is less legible than an honestly
  captioned static one.
- **Deposit sharing.** `run_extraction` gives every building the full `tc.resource_deposit[ri]`;
  a second site on the same deposit really does get the same richness. No adjustment.
- **Depletion taper.** A function of extracted-to-date, which is zero for a building that does not
  exist.

`corp_ai.cpp:239-249` keeps its inline crude duplicate (it omits habitability-scaled wages).
Switching it would change AI build scoring, hence world evolution, hence every blessed golden.
Known accepted divergence; add a comment pointing at the new function, change no behaviour.

### 2. Candidate model — one row per (type, target, recipe)

`processing_facility` expands into **one row per recipe** (`reg.recipe_count(processing_facility)`
= 3: steel, refined fuel, food rations). Their margins genuinely diverge, and `construct_building`
today hard-codes `reg.recipe_id("steel")` — so a single type-level bar priced at steel would report
"processing loses money here" while food rations is strongly profitable on the same tile. That is a
load-bearing figure silently misreporting.

The recipe therefore has to survive to construction. Seam, all additive and defaulted so no existing
caller changes:

- `ui_state::construction_state` gains `std::uint16_t pending_recipe = no_recipe;`
- `construct_building(...)` gains a trailing `std::uint16_t recipe = no_recipe`; where it sets
  `bc.recipe = reg.recipe_id("steel")` it becomes
  `bc.recipe = (recipe != no_recipe) ? recipe : reg.recipe_id("steel");`
- `app.cpp`'s pending drain passes it and clears it to `no_recipe` alongside `pending_tile`.

No save-format change: `building_component.recipe` is already serialised.

Row names must stay unique (the card's ImGui id is `c.name`): `"Processing: Steel"`,
`"Processing: Refined Fuel"`, `"Processing: Food Rations"` via a file-local `pretty_recipe()`
(underscores to spaces, title-case).

### 3. Row anatomy — the placeholder image is removed, not re-skinned

The 56x56 grey box is **deleted**. `charts::gutter` (40) alone exceeds it; nothing chart-like fits
there. Its 56 + 8 px of width is reclaimed by the row, which the column badly needs. Building
identity survives as an **18 px inline `icons::building` glyph** before the name.

Four lines per candidate card, at 278 px inner width (see § 4):

1. **Name** — 18 px glyph, then the name in `palette::selection`.
2. **Cost** — `TextDisabled`, credits **including material cost priced at the local market**, then,
   only when net > 0, ` · payback ~<n> ticks` (`capex / net`, `capex = build_cost + material_cost`;
   print `payback > 999 ticks` above that).
3. **Profit bar row**, 14 px tall — one of exactly three states:
   - *valid producing candidate*: `charts::draw_value_bar`, colour `palette::positive` /
     `palette::negative` / `palette::neutral` by sign of `net()`;
   - *valid non-producing* (Port, Launchpad, Inland Logistics Hub): no bar,
     `palette::neutral` text `"Infrastructure - no direct revenue; upkeep %.0f / tick"`;
   - *invalid candidate, or `has_data == false`*: no bar — the row's reason text occupies this slot.
4. **Action** — Build button (disabled + "Can't afford" when unaffordable) or the red
   `pr.message()`, exactly as today.

Roads keep their existing three-tier block unchanged and get **no** profit row (a road is a tile
mutation with no `building_component` and no upkeep in the model). Their placeholder box keeps its
tier-weighted line glyph; only their affordability gate is fixed.

**Sign encoding.** `charts::draw_bars`' `y_of(v)` inverts the rect for negative values and would
draw outside the clip box — a rendering bug, not a style choice. So bar **length encodes magnitude**
(`|net| / ceiling`), **colour encodes sign**, and the **signed value is printed in full**,
right-aligned, never elided. Because the list is sorted net-descending, every green sits above every
red, so the sign is obvious from position too.

**Shared ceiling** = `charts::tight_ceil(max |net|)` over the **valid producing candidates only**.
Invalid and infrastructure rows are excluded so they cannot inflate the axis and squash the bars
that matter. `tight_ceil` (not `nice_ceil`) keeps the tallest bar above ~70 % of the track.

**Caption**, once, above the list, `TextWrapped` in `palette::text_dim`:
`"Est. net / tick at today's local prices - 50% staffing, no labour shortage. Capex is not in the bar; see payback."`

### 4. Geometry — measured, not chosen

`charts::draw_bars` **cannot be used here**, and this is arithmetic rather than preference:

```
foldout_column_rect().w  = shell_column_width(disp.x) - nav_pane_width = 380 - 56 = 324   (the floor)
  - window WindowPadding 2x8                                                     = 308
  - ##build_list AlwaysVerticalScrollbar (ScrollbarSize 14)                      = 294
  - candidate card BeginChild(border=true) WindowPadding 2x8                     = 278   <- the design width
draw_bars: band = max(60, 278 - gutter(40) - legend_w(190)) = 60
```

60 px of plot for every column and gap. At 3+ bars it degenerates to 6 px stubs overflowing into
the legend — which is exactly why the tile accordion only ever passes two. Hand-rolling a bar in
`selection_panel.cpp` would break the "reuse the idiom" rule, so **extend `charts.{hpp,cpp}`** with
the primitive a narrow list actually needs. Per the Save-the-tool rule it then *is* the idiom
(BL-176's building table wants the same shape):

```cpp
/// One horizontal magnitude bar inside [mn, mx], for a narrow list where a clustered
/// vertical chart cannot fit (draw_bars reserves gutter + a 190px legend, exceeding the
/// fold-out column's ~278px row width). Length = |value| / ceiling; colour is the caller's;
/// the signed value prints right-aligned and is NEVER elided.
void draw_value_bar(ImDrawList* dl, ImVec2 mn, ImVec2 mx,
                    float value, float ceiling, ImU32 colour, const char* fmt = "%+.0f");
```

Internals: track `AddRectFilled(mn, mx, IM_COL32(48,50,58,255), 2.0f)`; value text measured with
`CalcTextSize`, `plot_w = (mx.x - mn.x) - std::max(52.0f, text_w) - 6.0f`; fill
`AddRectFilled({mn.x, mn.y}, {mn.x + plot_w * clamp(|value|/ceiling, 0, 1), mx.y}, colour, 2.0f)`;
a 2 px stub at the origin when `value == 0` or `ceiling <= 0` so zero reads as zero rather than as
absent; text right-aligned at `mx.x - text_w`, vertically centred, `IM_COL32(225,228,235,255)`.
Reserving `max(52, text_w)` means the figure can never be truncated **or** collide with the bar.

Row height, from the ImGui default style (`FramePadding {4,3}`, `ItemSpacing {4,4}`,
`WindowPadding {8,8}`):

```cpp
constexpr float bar_h = 14.0f;
const float row_h = style.WindowPadding.y * 2.0f
                  + ImGui::GetTextLineHeightWithSpacing()   // name
                  + ImGui::GetTextLineHeightWithSpacing()   // cost + payback
                  + bar_h + style.ItemSpacing.y             // profit bar
                  + ImGui::GetFrameHeight();                // Build / reason
```

≈ **87 px** (vs today's 80), pitch ≈ 95 px with the trailing `Spacing()`.

**Rows before scrolling.** Ledger height at 720 = `disp.y - profile_panel_height` = 628; header
block (title row 23 + separator 9 + Balance 17 + toast 17 + wrapped caption 30 + padding 16) ≈ 112;
list ≈ 516 → **5 rows fully visible, the 6th partial**. All 13 (4 extraction + 3 processing + 3
infrastructure + 3 road) fit by ~1150 px of display height. `##build_list` already carries
`AlwaysVerticalScrollbar` — keep it. Widths scale with `shell_column_width` (324 at the 380 floor
through 1900 px wide, 328 at 1920, 404 at the 460 cap); nothing is hard-coded to 324.

### 5. Sort order — confirmed, with a deterministic tail

`std::stable_sort` over the candidate vector, ties falling back to declaration order:

1. valid **producing** candidates, expected `net()` **descending**;
2. valid **infrastructure** (Port, Launchpad, Inland Logistics Hub), declaration order;
3. **invalid** candidates, declaration order;
4. **roads**, unchanged, in their own block after the list.

With recipe expansion the list is two screens deep at 720p, so the sort is what makes it usable —
the best five are the five you see without scrolling. `stable_sort` plus declaration-order ties
keeps the order frame-stable and free of any `unordered_map` iteration dependence.

### 6. Two defects fixed in the same pass

**(a) The affordability gate lies.** `selection_panel.cpp:1344` gates on `econ.build_cost` alone;
`construction.cpp:72` gates on `build_cost + material_cost`. Between those two figures the ledger
shows an **enabled** Build button that fails, with only a post-hoc toast, and materials print in raw
units the player cannot price. Mirror `construction.cpp:50-67`'s material sum, gate on the total,
and print the cost line as a **credit total**. Same fix on the road path (`:1424` vs
`construction.cpp:176-178`). Putting a precise profit bar next to a lying capex figure is worse than
either alone — and `payback` needs the true capex anyway.

**(b) A successful build closes the ledger.** `app.cpp:2690-2691` reassigns
`m_ui.selected_entity = built`, the selection stops being a tile, and `app.cpp:2665-2668` forces
`show_build_ledger = false`. Suppress that reassignment **when `m_ui.show_build_ledger` is true**
(canvas placement keeps its current behaviour). A rich tile stacks up to 4 extraction sites; a
comparison chart for one tile must survive a build. It also makes "Construction started." — written
to `ui.construction.last_message` and drawn at `selection_panel.cpp:1316` *inside the ledger that
just closed* — finally visible, and lets the chart re-evaluate against the newly occupied slot.

### 7. Constraints honoured

- **Container vocabulary.** No tenth container. The ledger is container 1, *Fold-out ledger column*
  (`LAYOUT.md:324`): wrap text policy (the caption uses `TextWrapped`), vertical-scroll overflow.
  The profit value is load-bearing and reserves its own measured width — never silently truncated.
- **Determinism.** `estimate_prospective_profit` is a pure read of `world` + `recipe_registry`; no
  RNG, no mutation, no lazy caches (the ledger holds `const world&`). Candidate order derives from
  `placement_rules::k_extractable`, a literal type list and the recipe vector — all stable
  sequences. (`body_mean_habitability` sums over an `unordered_map`; that FP-order sensitivity is
  pre-existing in `apply_budget` and is not made worse here.)
- **Glossary.** "/ tick" throughout, matching `draw_building_profit`'s existing
  "Profitability (est. / tick)" — GLOSSARY defines **Tick**; "qtr" is not a defined term. The same
  quantity must read identically before and after the build.
- **Trade.** The item's justification: it converts "here are things you may build" into "here is
  what each would earn", which is the decision that seeds every later trade the building feeds.

### Decisions taken on Ben's behalf (2026-07-30)

Ben authorised proceeding without the owed mockup; every proportion below is settled, not proposed.

1. **`estimate_building_profit` cannot serve a hypothetical** — verified in code (needs both an
   existing entity and a report row). New pure `estimate_prospective_profit` added beside it, taking
   no `economy_report`, so `draw_construction_ledger`'s signature and its one call site are untouched.
2. **One bar per candidate, not per type** — `processing_facility` expands into its 3 recipes. Cost
   is a defaulted `recipe` param on `construct_building` plus a `pending_recipe` field; benefit is
   that the chart stops misreporting processing, and the recipe becomes a build-time choice.
3. **Non-producing types get no bar**, only their upkeep in words, reusing
   `draw_building_selection`'s existing "earns through what it enables" framing.
4. **Invalid candidates stay, greyed, with the reason, and are excluded from the ceiling** — BL-071's
   reason vocabulary is the ledger's teaching surface; dropping rows destroys it.
5. **Sort by net descending confirmed**, with infrastructure then invalid then roads as a
   deterministic tail.
6. **`charts::draw_bars` overturned as the primitive** — measured at 60 px of usable band in a 278 px
   row. Added `charts::draw_value_bar` (horizontal magnitude bar) to `charts.{hpp,cpp}` instead of
   hand-rolling, so it becomes the reusable idiom for narrow lists.
7. **Negative nets: magnitude length + sign colour + full signed number** — `draw_bars` has no
   negative axis and would draw outside its clip box.
8. **Per tick, not per quarter** — GLOSSARY defines Tick; the figure must match the built building's.
9. **No price-response, deposit-sharing or depletion modelling** — stated in the caption rather than
   half-modelled.
10. **Payback added** as one text token on the cost line; net alone ignores capex.
11. **Affordability gate fixed to include material cost** (buildings and roads) — the chart's
    companion figure must be as truthful as the chart.
12. **The ledger now stays open after a successful build** when it is the surface that initiated it.
13. **`corp_ai.cpp` deliberately left alone** — refactoring it would change AI scoring, world
    evolution and every blessed golden, for no player-visible gain.

### Decisions taken on Ben's behalf (2026-07-30)

Ben delegated these calls for the ultracode session and was unavailable; each is recorded here so it can be reviewed or overturned.

**Q. Is the SELECTION.md claim true — does draw_construction_ledger already list, cost, reason-code and build?**

- **Decision:** VERIFIED TRUE. The backlog prose is stale; SELECTION.md is right.
- **Why:** Read src/ui/selection_panel.cpp:1265-1480 directly. Candidate enumeration :1323-1332, cost :1364-1369, placement_rules::can_place_in_world + pr.message() :1342/:1390, Build writing ui.construction.pending_tile/type/target :1375-1380, drained by app.cpp:2675-2705 into the real construct_building. The only placeholder is the 56x56 grey box at :1350-1357 (road twin :1430-1436). Remaining scope is exactly the chart, plus two adjacent defects the chart makes intolerable (below).

**Q. Can estimate_building_profit be evaluated for a hypothetical building on an empty tile?**

- **Decision:** NO — it is doubly blocked. Add a new exported sibling: estimate_prospective_profit(const world&, const recipe_registry&, entity_id tile, building_type, resource_type target, uint16_t recipe_id = no_recipe) in world/building_profit.{hpp,cpp}.
- **Why:** building_profit.cpp:14-17 requires w.buildings.find(id) to hit, and :20-24 requires a matching report.buildings row; either miss returns has_data=false. Its revenue is br->output_quantity — a REALISED figure, not a model. The prospective function takes no economy_report, so draw_construction_ledger's signature and its single call site (app.cpp:2666) are untouched. It is a pure read of world+registry: no RNG, no caches, no mutation, safe in world/ under the determinism rule.

**Q. What workforce/contention/habitability assumptions does the prospective estimate make?**

- **Decision:** workforce_assigned = 0.5 (0.0 for port and inland_logistics_hub), workforce_target = 100, contention scalar = 1.0, habitability = body_mean_habitability(w, body). Opex via the real compute_building_opex on a stack-local synthetic building_component.
- **Why:** 0.5/0.0 mirrors construction.cpp:84-85 exactly, so the estimate describes the building that will actually be created. 100 is building_component's own default. Contention 1.0 because no economy_report is in hand and the true scalar depends on a labour pool the new building has not yet joined — assume no shortage and SAY SO in the caption rather than fabricate. Using compute_building_opex + body_mean_habitability (rather than corp_ai.cpp:246's cruder ex.maintenance + ex.base_wage*wf) gives exact parity with apply_budget, so the pre-build number and the post-build Net in draw_building_profit agree.

**Q. One bar per building TYPE or per candidate RECIPE?**

- **Decision:** Per candidate = (type, target, recipe). Extraction expands per deposited resource (already does); processing_facility expands into one row per recipe (steel / refined fuel / food rations); port, launchpad and inland_logistics_hub are one row each.
- **Why:** recipe_registry::recipe_count(processing_facility) returns all 3 recipes and their margins genuinely diverge — food rations on an agricultural tile versus steel is a different proposition entirely. construct_building currently HARD-CODES reg.recipe_id("steel") (construction.cpp), so a single type-level bar priced at steel would tell the player 'processing loses money here' when a different recipe is strongly profitable. That is a load-bearing figure silently misreporting, which LAYOUT.md forbids in spirit. Cost of honesty is small: a defaulted uint16_t recipe param on construct_building plus a pending_recipe field. It also fixes a real wart — you currently cannot choose a recipe at build time, only switch it afterwards.

**Q. How do non-producing types (Port, Launchpad, Inland Logistics Hub) appear?**

- **Decision:** Valid, buildable, but NO bar. Their bar row prints, in palette::neutral: 'Infrastructure - no direct revenue; upkeep <n> / tick'. They are excluded from the shared ceiling and sort below the producing candidates.
- **Why:** Their honest net is -maintenance-wages, strictly negative. A large red bar for a Port would actively mislead — a port is an enabler, not a bad investment. draw_building_selection already says this in words ('Infrastructure - produces nothing directly / It earns through what it enables, not what it makes'); reuse that vocabulary rather than plot a number that means the opposite of what it looks like. Naming the upkeep keeps a real figure on screen.

**Q. Do invalid candidates render greyed with the reason, or drop out of the chart?**

- **Decision:** KEPT, greyed, reason text shown — bar SUPPRESSED, and excluded from the shared ceiling. They sink to the bottom of the list.
- **Why:** Teaching WHY you cannot build here is the entire point of BL-071's reason vocabulary; dropping the row destroys the lesson and makes the ledger's contents flicker as world state changes. But a profit bar for something unbuildable is noise AND it would inflate the shared ceiling, squashing the bars that matter. So: row stays, reason stays, bar goes.

**Q. Sort order — confirm or overturn 'by profit descending'?**

- **Decision:** CONFIRMED, with an explicit deterministic tail: (1) valid producing candidates by expected net DESCENDING; (2) valid infrastructure in declaration order (Port, Launchpad, Hub); (3) invalid candidates in declaration order; (4) roads last, in their own unchanged block. std::stable_sort, ties break to declaration order.
- **Why:** With recipe expansion a rich tile now yields up to 10 building rows plus 3 road rows against ~5 visible at 720p — the sort is what makes a two-screen list usable, because the best five are the five you see without scrolling. stable_sort plus declaration-order ties keeps the list frame-to-frame stable and deterministic (no unordered_map iteration in the ordering).

**Q. Exact chart geometry, reusing the charts.cpp idiom.**

- **Decision:** OVERTURNED the vertical-clustered assumption. charts::draw_bars CANNOT fit this column. Instead add ONE new primitive to charts.{hpp,cpp} — charts::draw_value_bar (a horizontal magnitude bar) — and draw it inline in each candidate card. Geometry: row inner width 278 px at the 380 floor; bar track 14 px tall spanning the row width less max(52, text_w)+6 reserved for the right-aligned signed value; shared ceiling = charts::tight_ceil(max |net| over valid producing candidates); colour palette::positive / negative / neutral by sign. row_h ~= 87 px; ~5 rows visible at 1280x720, all 13 by ~1150 px tall; the list already has AlwaysVerticalScrollbar.
- **Why:** Hard measurement, not preference. foldout_column_rect().w = 380-56 = 324 at the floor; minus window padding 308; minus the list's 14 px scrollbar 294; minus the bordered row card's padding 278. charts::draw_bars computes band = max(60, (mx.x - mn.x) - gutter(40) - legend_w(190)) = 62 px for ALL bars plus gaps — it degenerates to 6 px stubs overflowing into the legend at anything past 2 columns. That is why the tile accordion only ever passes 2. Hand-rolling in selection_panel.cpp would violate 'reuse the idiom', so instead EXTEND charts.hpp with the primitive a narrow list actually needs; per the Save-the-tool rule it then IS the idiom, and BL-176's building table wants the same thing.

**Q. How are negative expected nets drawn, given draw_bars has no negative axis? (question the code forced; not in the brief)**

- **Decision:** Bar length encodes MAGNITUDE (|net| / ceiling); colour encodes sign (palette::positive / palette::negative); the signed value is printed in full, right-aligned, never elided or truncated.
- **Why:** draw_bars' y_of(v) inverts the rect for v<0 and would draw below the baseline outside the clip box — a genuine rendering bug, not a styling choice. Magnitude+sign-colour is an established legible convention, and because the list is sorted net-descending all greens sit above all reds, making the sign obvious from position alone. The exact number is always present, satisfying LAYOUT.md's no-silent-truncation rule for a load-bearing figure.

**Q. Per tick or per quarter?**

- **Decision:** PER TICK. Caption and values read '/ tick', matching draw_building_profit's existing 'Profitability (est. / tick)'.
- **Why:** GLOSSARY.md defines Tick ('the fixed period between economy updates'); it does not define 'qtr'. The standing rule forbids substituting an alternative for a defined term. Decisive tiebreaker: the same quantity must read identically before and after the build, so the candidate's number is directly comparable to the built building's Net in the Selection band.

**Q. Does the estimate model price response, deposit sharing with existing sites, or the depletion taper? (question the code forced)**

- **Decision:** NO to all three. Pure 'at today's local prices, fresh deposit' read, stated in the caption.
- **Why:** run_extraction gives each building the full tc.resource_deposit[ri], so no sharing adjustment is correct, not an omission. The depletion taper is a function of extracted-to-date, which is zero for a building that does not exist. Price response (adding supply depresses price) is modelled nowhere in the build path today — solve_workforce_target has wf_target_price but the AI's build scorer does not — and a half-modelled elasticity is less legible than an honestly-captioned static one. Stated explicitly so nobody 'improves' it into divergence.

**Q. Should the ledger also show payback? (not in the brief)**

- **Decision:** YES — one right-aligned token on the cost line: 'payback ~<n> ticks', shown only when net > 0.
- **Why:** Net alone ranks by earnings and ignores capex; corp_ai.cpp:248 already uses capex/net as its own decision figure. Four lines of text, no new geometry, and it converts 'which earns most' into 'which is worth it'.

**Q. Fix the affordability defect (Build enabled when balance cannot cover materials)? (recon finding, not in the brief)**

- **Decision:** YES, in this item. Mirror construction.cpp:50-67's material_cost and gate on build_cost + material_cost; print the cost line as a credit total.
- **Why:** selection_panel.cpp:1344 gates on econ.build_cost alone while construction.cpp:72 gates on build_cost + material_cost, so an enabled Build button can fail with only a post-hoc toast, and materials print in raw units the player cannot price. Putting a precise profit bar beside a lying capex figure is worse than either alone — the chart makes the return legible, so the cost must become legible in the same pass. Road path (:1424) has the identical bug; fix both.

**Q. Fix the ledger closing itself on a successful build? (recon finding, not in the brief)**

- **Decision:** YES. On construction_result::placed, suppress the m_ui.selected_entity = built reassignment WHEN m_ui.show_build_ledger is true; leave the canvas-placement path unchanged.
- **Why:** app.cpp:2690-2691 reselects the new building, which makes sel non-tile, which makes app.cpp:2665-2668 force show_build_ledger = false. A rich tile stacks up to 4 extraction sites; a comparison chart whose whole purpose is evaluating candidates on ONE tile must survive a build. It also means 'Construction started.' (written to ui.construction.last_message and drawn at selection_panel.cpp:1316 inside the ledger that just closed) is finally visible, and the chart re-evaluates against the newly-occupied slot.

**Q. Does this need a tenth LAYOUT.md container?**

- **Decision:** NO. The construction ledger is container 1, the Fold-out ledger column: wrap text policy, vertical-scroll overflow.
- **Why:** It is positioned by foldout_column_rect() into the fold-out column slot. TextWrapped for the caption is the correct policy for that container; the numeric profit value is load-bearing and reserves its own measured width, so it is never truncated. No new container kind is invented.

**Q. Refactor corp_ai.cpp's inline duplicate of this formula to call the new function?**

- **Decision:** NO. Leave corp_ai.cpp untouched; add a one-line comment pointing at estimate_prospective_profit and note the divergence.
- **Why:** The AI's version omits habitability-scaled wages, so switching it would change AI build scoring, which changes world evolution, which invalidates every blessed golden. Deterministic-world risk with zero player-visible payoff in this item. Named as a known accepted divergence rather than silently ignored.

items.title: On-canvas legends need smooth scrolling for overflowing entry lists
items.completion_note: Landed 2026-07-10 (also resolves [[BL-163]], folded per Ben). Added a shared draw_scroll_list_key helper in body_surface_canvas.cpp: a dark panel with a fixed header (+ optional good-selector combo for the Market lens) over a bounded, wheel/drag-scrolling borderless ImGui child hosting the rows (the draw_lens_resource_combo pattern). Box height is capped to the canvas vertical span [grid_top+8, canvas_bottom-8] passed from the caller and clamped in-bounds, so a long list scrolls instead of overrunning. Converted the four count-driven keys (Country/Market/Reach/Supply) onto it via a key_row{marker_colour,label_colour,label,key_marker,bar_frac} vocabulary (swatch/dot/bar markers). Verified by capture: Country lens now shows its full ~20-nation list bounded within the canvas (was clipped off-bottom); Market combo+swatch list intact. Goldens for the changed lenses (country_lens, market_lens, and reach/supply where the key renders) need re-blessing on Linux CI — the change is intentional. Authority propagated to LENSES.md.
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-10 (Ben ideas thread). Legends in general (the on-canvas lens legends in body_surface_canvas.cpp) should scroll smoothly when their entry list exceeds the available height, rather than overflowing or being clipped. Generalises the fix in [[BL-163]] from the Resource lens to all lens legends.
items.design: **Give the on-canvas lens legends a scrollable body.** Where a legend's entry list can exceed the reserved height (Country with many nations, Market with many markets, Resource with deposit bands), host the entry rows in a bounded, smoothly-scrolling ImGui child (window flags for a clean scrollbar; the existing scrollable BeginCombo at body_surface_canvas.cpp:137 is precedent for hosting scroll chrome inside a legend). Keep the legend header/title fixed and scroll only the rows. Smooth (pixel/wheel) scroll, not paged. Shared helper across the per-lens legend builders so the behaviour is uniform. Supersedes the box-sizing half-measure in [[BL-163]] for the overflow case — sequence so BL-163's quick overlap fix lands first, then this generalises. Authority → LENSES.md on landing. Ben ideas thread 2026-07-10.

items.title: Selection-aware descend hotkey — Enter dives into the current selection down the zoom ladder
items.completion_note: Landed in commit 82e00f4 (2026-07-10): canvas_command::descend made selection-aware, routing a surface-bearing selection through focus_on_entity; blind rung-drop retained as the no-selection fallback. Verify: scripts/verify/descend_into_selection.lua (blessed). Status reconciled 2026-07-10 (was stale at 'designed' after the work committed).
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-10 (Ben ideas thread). SCOPE NARROWED at design (2026-07-10): keyboard ladder navigation ALREADY EXISTS — app.cpp binds Enter=descend rung, Backspace=ascend rung, [ / ]=prev/next body (all in the F1 key-binding help). The real gap is that canvas_command::descend is a BLIND primary_level rung-drop that ignores the selection, so single-click-a-body-then-Enter does not dive into that body. This item makes the descend hotkey selection-aware. Scroll-past-zoom NOT pursued (Ben's call, 2026-07-10, hotkeys-only).
items.design: **Settled (Ben, hotkeys-only, 2026-07-10).** Finding at design time: the zoom-ladder hotkeys the original idea asked for already exist — `app.cpp` key table binds **Enter → canvas_command::descend**, **Backspace → ascend**, **[ / ] → body_prev/next**, surfaced in the F1 help. So this is NOT 'add hotkeys'. The gap: `apply_canvas_command`'s `descend` (canvas_command.cpp:81) is a **blind** `primary_level` rung-drop — it descends the foregrounded canvas on the *previously-anchored* body, ignoring `ui.selected_entity`. After the single-click-selects model (SELECTION.md), the natural gesture is **click a body, press Enter to dive into it** — but today Enter drops a rung on the old anchor instead. **Change:** make `descend` **selection-aware** — when `ui.selected_entity` resolves to a descendable entity (body/tile via the same probe `focus_on_entity` uses), route through **`focus_on_entity(w, ui, selected_entity)`** so it re-anchors to the selection and descends to its most informative rung (identical to the double-click / panel 'go to' path). Fall back to the existing blind rung-drop when there is **no** selection (or it is non-descendable — e.g. the star, or a tile already on Planetary), so bare Enter still works as today. **Ascend (Backspace) unchanged.** Deterministic; adds no new hit-testing. **Not pursued:** scroll-past-max-zoom (Ben chose hotkeys-only) — parked as a possible future feel enhancement, not part of this item. Authority → CANVASES.md on landing (note the descend gesture is now selection-driven). Ben ideas thread + design pass 2026-07-10.

items.title: Split agriculture for interplanetary use — terrestrial vs off-world food production
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-10 (Ben ideas thread). Concept: agriculture/food production should split into a terrestrial form and a controlled-environment form, so that feeding population where terrestrial affinities are absent is mechanically distinct from Earth-like farming. Re-settled 2026-07-21: gated by habitability/terrain, not tech era — valid on any tile lacking the terrestrial affinities, not just off-world. Same raw good as terrestrial farming, distinct recipe/building. Corrected 2026-07-21 (BL-190): the population agricultural_produce demand pass already exists live in economy_system.cpp — this item is buildable now, not blocked on a future consumer.
items.design:
**Idea — design owed.** Today agriculture is a single terrain-affinity extraction (RESOURCES.md / PRODUCTION.md). The proposal: farming that feeds population where terrestrial affinities (arable land, water/river adjacency, climate) are absent should be a distinct recipe/building — a controlled-environment / hydroponic food building consuming refined inputs (energy, water, structural goods) rather than raw terrain. Relates to [[BL-168]] (coastal fishing — the other food-source idea). Authority → RESOURCES.md / PRODUCTION.md when designed. Ben ideas thread 2026-07-10.

### Settled 2026-07-21 (Ben) — supersedes the 2026-07-21 (round 1) Era-1 framing
**Gate: habitability/terrain, not tech era.** Ben's call: this is not an Era-1/space concern. A **Hydroponics Bay** is valid on **any tile lacking the terrestrial farming affinities** — arable land, water/river adjacency ([[BL-170]]), climate — regardless of body or era. On the Earth-like homeworld that means arid/barren tiles unsuited to the terrestrial Farm; off-world it means every tile, since none carry the terrestrial affinities at all. Decouples this item from the Era 0/Era 1 gate (ERAS.md) entirely — habitability/terrain is the authority, not era.

**One good, distinct recipe.** The Hydroponics Bay produces the same raw-tier **Agricultural produce** the terrestrial Farm already does (RESOURCES.md), consuming refined inputs (energy, water, structural goods) instead of terrain affinity — feeds the existing Food Processor → Food rations chain with no new resource or market fragmentation. Alongside [[BL-168]] (fishing), Agricultural produce is a raw good with three alternate producers (Farm, Hydroponics Bay, Fishing Wharf), one shared refined output.

### Corrected 2026-07-21 (BL-190)
The 'lacks a food consumer' framing above was wrong — `economy_system.cpp`'s population-demand pass already adds live `agricultural_produce` market demand per population centre every tick ([[BL-190]]). This item is **buildable now**: a Hydroponics Bay recipe/building against the existing terrain-habitability predicate and the existing raw→refined chain, no population-model dependency left.

items.title: Planetology — generated atmosphere, chemistry, and a simulated evolution history (Shadow Empire-inspired)
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-10 as 'climate modelling', re-settled 2026-07-21 (Sprint 1 procgen review) into a much larger, un-parked, higher-priority vision: a body-level Planetology phase — generated atmosphere composition, basic chemistry, and a simulated abiogenesis/evolution history — explicitly modelled on Shadow Empire's planet generation. Ben: 'this is going to be the first thing a player sees, so it has to impress them.' New authority doc docs/generation/PLANETOLOGY.md; lands as a sibling pass per BL-051's pipeline-shape decision.
items.design:
**Idea — parked, design owed (original framing).** Tile generation already derives static solar parameters per body (temperature class, atmosphere class, hydrological state, geological activity — TILE_GENERATION.md) and bands oceans by a noise height field. This idea originally proposed a climate model: latitude/altitude-driven temperature and moisture bands. Ben ideas thread 2026-07-10.

### Re-settled 2026-07-21 (Ben, Sprint 1 procgen review) — supersedes the original 'climate modelling' framing
**Reframed as Planetology: a body-level history/chemistry pass, not just a tile-level climate band.** Ben's explicit reference is **Shadow Empire's** planet generation (VR Designs/Slitherine) — researched this session. Shadow Empire generates each world through three phases: **Planetology** (astrophysical rolls — age, gravity, temperature, water retention, initial atmosphere composition), **Geology** (terrain/rainfall derived from the Planetology rolls), and a simulated **Evolution** phase (hundreds of millions of years of abiogenesis-gated biological history, listing any species that arose and went extinct before colonisation). Atmospheric composition is explicitly **impacted by the emergence of life** — a planet with a thriving biosphere reads ~15% oxygen; a planet where abiogenesis conditions were never met keeps a sterile, thinner atmosphere and may lack fossil fuels entirely. This is the model Ben wants Project Io's body generation to work toward, because — his words — it's 'the first thing a player sees' and has to carry real first-impression weight.

**Scope for this item:**
1. **Initial atmosphere generation** — derive a per-body atmosphere composition (gas mix, not just the current single `atmosphere_class` enum) from basic chemistry: the body's solar parameters (temperature class, geological activity, water retention) set the starting inorganic mix (CO2/N2/H2O vapour/trace gases), same spirit as Shadow Empire's Planetology roll.
2. **A simulated abiogenesis/evolution pass** — gate life's emergence on chemistry preconditions (liquid water, temperature band, energy source), and if met, simulate a coarse evolutionary history (an abstracted timeline, not a creature simulator) that produces a body-level biosphere-richness outcome and a habitability/oxygen-level consequence.
3. **Atmosphere changes as a consequence of that history** — oxygen and other biogenic gases shift the generated atmosphere mix based on whether/how much life emerged, mirroring Shadow Empire's life-alters-atmosphere link. This is still a **one-time generation-time computation** producing a fixed history and a resulting atmosphere state, not an ongoing tick-by-tick weather/climate simulation — deterministic and bounded, per the standing seeded-generation rule.
4. **Presentation** — since this is the player's first impression, the body's generated history (its Planetology/Evolution 'backstory') needs a legible surface, likely a short generated-history readout at body selection/campaign start, not just backing data. Exact UI surface is open — flag for a follow-up design pass once the generation model itself is scoped in TECH detail.

**Architecture: a sibling pass.** Per BL-051's settled pipeline-shape decision this sprint, this is a **body-level sibling pass** invoked outside/before the six-pass tile pipeline (Planetology logically precedes Geology, i.e. tile generation, in Shadow Empire's own ordering) — not a modification to the six-pass core.

**Authority: new doc.** This is a body-level history/chemistry system, a distinct concern from tile-level terrain generation — gets its own authority doc, **docs/generation/PLANETOLOGY.md**, cross-referenced from TILE_GENERATION.md (which it now precedes) and GENERATION_STRATEGY.md (the cross-cutting generation map). Doc creation is this item's own delivery, not scoped here.

**Priority/parking: un-parked, raised to B.** Ben's call: this is no longer a speculative maybe — it's a first-impression pillar for the game, reprioritized accordingly. Still **post-v0.1.0** (a body-history/chemistry system is real scope beyond the prototype's economy-loop arc), but now a real, committed post-prototype item, not a parked one.

**Determinism.** Hard requirement, unchanged — the Planetology/Evolution pass must be a pure deterministic function of the campaign seed, same as every other generation pass (io-standing-rules.md).

**Open for the next design pass (not settled here):** the exact chemistry model's fidelity (how detailed 'basic chemistry' goes), the evolutionary-history abstraction's shape (a fixed set of possible history 'archetypes' vs a richer simulated timeline), and the presentation surface named in point 4.

### R&D pass landed 2026-07-21 (Sprint 1) — chemistry researched, calls owed
**The chemical chain from (A) input solar system → (B) life → (C) civilisation is now modelled end to end** in the authority doc, docs/generation/PLANETOLOGY.md. Ten gated stages (System → Accretion → Air → Engine → Water → Spark → Breath → Green → Legacy → Spend), each a threshold test on already-computed scalars rather than a simulation, each emitting one dated timeline line. Researched across 13 domains with an adversarial fact-check per domain; real quantitative anchors throughout (cosmic shoreline v_esc^4/S normalised to Mars=1.0 reproducing the observed 11-body split; Kopparapu S_eff limits 1.0512/0.3438; radiogenic effective half-life 2.06 Gyr; ozone full-shield at 5–10% PAL not 1%; oil window 60–120 C; ~90% of coal beds in one ~107 Myr window; copper needing 150–350x concentration against iron’s 5–12x).

**The B→C joint — the part Ben specifically asked about — is concrete, not hand-waved.** A biosphere physically manufactures the industrial base: banded iron (>60% of world iron reserves, window OPENING with an Fe-oxidising biosphere and CLOSING at deep-ocean oxidation), petroleum (marine algal, so gated on microbial-not-complex life), coal (land plants + everwet basins + subsidence), bauxite/laterite and supergene copper (both requiring free O2), and soil (requiring biological nitrogen fixation). No life, no coal. Microbes only, and you get colossal iron and real oil but no forests, no soil, and no fire.

**Homeworld rule settled in shape:** constrain the INPUTS (sample the homeworld orbit/mass/water from the sub-region where the identical unmodified chain succeeds), never clamp the gates or the outputs. Variation comes from gate MARGINS, chiefly the iron/coal antagonism — one number (when the deep ocean stopped being ferruginous) trades iron against coal in opposite directions with every gate passed.

**11 open calls are recorded in the doc and are Ben’s, not settled.** The two load-bearing ones: (1) at current scope the feature produces ONE interesting body — Cinder/Selene/Pallas all terminate at stage 1–3 and Kepler is the constrained homeworld, so six of thirteen archetypes and the whole S5–S8 ladder are dead code until world_params::body_count is activated; (2) deposit_scalar (BL-114) ownership must be reconciled before implementation, not discovered at merge. Also flagged: the model is honest that its endowment framing is a game contrivance and that several load-bearing thresholds (BIF oxidant, abiogenesis probability, fire minimum, ozone gate) sit on contested science.

### Landed 2026-07-21/22 — the chain, and the New World wizard
**Shipped.** `src/world/planetology.{hpp,cpp}`: ten gated stages (System, Accretion, Air, Engine,
Water, Spark, Breath, Green, Legacy, Spend) as a sibling pass run before generate_body_tiles, per
BL-051's convention. Each stage is a threshold test on already-computed scalars, not a simulation,
and emits one dated history line; the interesting output is which gate a body died at.

**It derives the body_profile** that used to be four hand-authored literals in hard_coded_world.cpp.
23 of 24 fields reproduce the authored values exactly (Kepler bit-identical, so the homeworld surface
is unchanged). The single divergence is Cinder's geological_activity: authored 'high', derives 'low'
— Mercury is genuinely geologically dead and the authored value was flavour. Costs Cinder some
mountain/rift cluster seeds.

**Two tile-pipeline hooks**, both taking an optional const planetology_state* so a null state
reproduces the pre-BL-167 surface bit-for-bit: a biotic composition mask in Pass 4 (falling back to
composition_abiotic, which mirrors the biotic branch's RNG consumption draw-for-draw so the two stay
stream-aligned), and the per-resource endowment multiply in Pass 6 alongside deposit_scalar.

**Ben's calls.** (1) 'One planet with life is much better for what I'm imagining' — the unreachable
archetype rungs are the intended shape, not a gap; closes the dead-code open call. (2) The one-shot
flow became a per-stage WIZARD: 'I would prefer that the user sees each stage and chooses at each
stage. This helps the user see how the process works and makes it more impressive.' Presented with
charts in the tile-selection idiom.

**The wizard** (app.cpp): ten stages, each with an explainer of the actual chemistry, live charts of
the system as it currently stands, and that stage's decision. Air and Legacy carry NO knob — the
first is a consequence of earlier choices, the second is the payoff — and the UI says so rather than
inventing one. Four new decision points beyond the original six: home_mass, radiogenic,
abiogenesis_ease, coal_climate. radiogenic is deliberately independent of metallicity (U/Th come from
rare r-process events, so a metal-rich system need not be geologically live).

**Charts** are src/ui/charts.{hpp,cpp}, EXTRACTED from the tile-selection deposit graphs (BL-123) so
both surfaces share one implementation rather than imitating each other. Verified pixel-neutral: the
tile golden's diff is byte-identical to the figure measured before the refactor (4.7980%, which is
pre-existing staleness, not this change). Adds tight_ceil (a finer axis ladder than nice_ceil),
threshold_line (a gate drawn on the same axis as the values it judges), and an explicit bar_cap so
wide charts auto-fit while the tile graphs keep their mockup-fixed 34px columns.

**Shared prototype body set.** The four bodies' authored physical facts live once, in planetology.cpp,
reached via prototype_body()/prototype_body_seed(). make_hard_coded_world and the wizard's live
preview_system() walk the same list with the same seeds, so the charts a player decides against
cannot drift from the world actually built.

**Verification: tools/verify/planetology_harness.cpp**, auto-registered as a CTest. R1 determinism,
R2 archetypes + derived profiles, R3 the B->C joint (no life no coal; no aqueous history no clay;
airless bodies keep polar ice), R4 the iron/coal antagonism with both dial ends still passing every
gate, R5 the homeworld corridor across the whole knob space (100/100), R6 WIZARD STABILITY (a
decision at stage N never rewrites the history of a stage before N — what makes Back/Continue safe,
asserted for all seven knobs), R7 every new knob moves its own outcome. Visual check:
scripts/verify/planetology_generation.lua captures all ten wizard stages plus the menu and the
resulting surface. All 22 CTest targets pass.

**The harness caught five real defects before the feature was ever seen:** Selene's tidal term
overflowed to ~3e11 (raw AU fed into an a^-7.5 exponent), Cinder was mis-banded a whole temperature
class by a wet-planet albedo on bare rock, Selene grew clay it cannot have, Pallas reported 0 K by
exiting before instellation was computed, and the iron endowment saturated its clamp so both ends of
the oxygenation dial returned the same number.

**Known dormancy.** The biotic terrain mask has no body to fire on in the shipped set — it only bites
on a world that HAS an atmosphere yet never reached land, and Kepler is the only atmospheric body and
always lives. Built, correct, and exercised by a synthetic small-wet-world case in the harness.

**Still open** (PLANETOLOGY.md § Open calls): deposit_scalar (BL-114) ownership vs the endowment,
resource-list expansion (limestone has the strongest case), spatial ore provinces vs body-level
scalars, survey-gating the report, the report's permanent home, the fire threshold as hard gate vs
soft penalty, and whether the homeworld's joint iron/fuel floor is stated or hidden.

items.title: Coastal fishing — a coastal-terrain food/resource extraction
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-10 (Ben ideas thread). Concept: a fishing extraction building valid on coastal tiles (land adjacent to ocean), producing food — giving coastline mechanical value and a terrain-gated food source distinct from inland agriculture. Re-settled 2026-07-21: fishing itself feeds the same Agricultural produce good as farming, via a runtime coastal-adjacency check; the broader coastal identity (ports/sea trade, coastal defense) spun off into [[BL-188]] and [[BL-189]] rather than widening this item. Corrected 2026-07-21 (BL-190): buildable now — the population agricultural_produce demand pass already exists live.
items.design:
**Idea — design owed.** A fishing building placeable on **coastal** tiles (land adjacent to an ocean tile) that extracts a food resource, giving coastline value and diversifying food sourcing beyond inland agriculture. Requires a notion of coastal adjacency the terrain model does not currently expose as a placement predicate (TILES.md has the two-axis composition×landform model and noise-banded oceans — coastal = land tile bordering ocean). Authority → PRODUCTION.md / TILES.md when designed. Ben ideas thread 2026-07-10.

### Settled 2026-07-21 (Ben) — supersedes the 2026-07-21 (round 1) settle
**Same good, own recipe.** A **Fishing Wharf** produces the same raw-tier **Agricultural produce** as the Farm and [[BL-166]]'s Hydroponics Bay — one shared good, three alternate producers, no market fragmentation.

**Coastal-adjacency predicate: runtime neighbor check**, not a precomputed per-tile flag — at placement-check time, test whether any of the tile's 6 hex neighbours is ocean composition. Cheap, always correct, and reusable by other coastal buildings without adding stored state — including [[BL-188]] (ports) and [[BL-189]] (coastal defense), which read the same predicate rather than each inventing their own.

**Scope kept narrow.** Ben's call: fishing itself stays this item's scope; the wider coastal-identity ideas he raised in this round — sea trade/ports, coastal military positioning — are big enough to be their own items, not a widening of BL-168. Filed as [[BL-188]] (Ports/sea trade) and [[BL-189]] (Coastal defense stub note), both keyed to this item's coastal-adjacency predicate.

### Corrected 2026-07-21 (BL-190)
The 'lacks a food consumer' framing above was wrong — the population-demand pass already adds live `agricultural_produce` market demand ([[BL-190]]). Buildable now against the existing raw→refined chain and the runtime coastal predicate above.

items.title: Feasibility study — alternative solar-system geometry / body configuration
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-10 (Ben ideas thread). Concept/feasibility: whether the game could support solar-system geometries other than the current hard-coded Earth-like arrangement — different numbers/positions of bodies, orbital layouts, or non-standard configurations — and what the generation and canvas layers would need. A scoping/feasibility question, not a build item.
items.design: **Feasibility question — no build yet.** The world is a seeded, hard-coded Earth-like solar system (make_hard_coded_world; TILE_GENERATION.md prototype body profiles). This item asks how feasible **alternative solar geometry** is — different body counts, orbital arrangements, or non-Earth-like configurations — and what it would cost across the Solar canvas layout (CANVASES.md / SOLAR.md), the zoom ladder, generation, and determinism. Deliverable of this item is a **feasibility note**, not code: what is parameterised vs hard-coded today, what would have to generalise, and whether it feeds a mechanic (Trade/Conflict) or is variety for its own sake. **Parked (F), post-v0.1.0** — the prototype validates the economy loop on the fixed world; solar-geometry variation is out of scope until then. Revisit as a scoping exercise, not a feature, when the prototype is cut. Authority → GENERATION_STRATEGY.md. Ben ideas thread 2026-07-10.

items.title: Rivers & freshwater generation — surface hydrology on the tile map
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-10 (Ben ideas thread). Concept: generate rivers / freshwater on the tile map. Today hydrology is only a per-body hydrological state plus noise-banded oceans (TILE_GENERATION.md); there is no surface freshwater feature. Re-settled 2026-07-21: a river is an edge feature (borders exactly two tiles, never occupies one — a lake would be the tile-occupying counterpart), directional (upstream/downstream), and gives the tile it borders a cheaper logistics traversal weight — a distinct mechanic from the original tile-flag/adjacency-only framing.
items.design:
**Idea — design owed.** Surface hydrology today is coarse: a per-body hydrological state and noise-banded oceans (TILE_GENERATION.md six-pass pipeline); there are no rivers and no inland freshwater. This item proposes generating **rivers** across the tile map, most naturally as a downhill trace over the existing height field (the same noise field that bands oceans), from high ground to ocean/basin. Sits with [[BL-167]] (climate) as the hydrology/climate enrichment cluster. Authority → TILE_GENERATION.md when designed. Ben ideas thread 2026-07-10.

### Settled 2026-07-21 (Ben) — supersedes the 2026-07-21 (round 1) tile-flag settle
**A river is an edge, not a tile.** Ben's call: a river borders **exactly two tiles** — it never occupies a tile itself (that would be a lake, a distinct, unrelated feature — not scoped here). Generation is unchanged in spirit (a downhill trace over the height field, high ground → ocean/basin) but the trace now walks the tile **edge graph**: each traced step marks the shared edge between the two tiles it crosses, not the tile itself. Storage: a per-tile bitmask of which of its 6 hex sides border a river reads cheaply from either tile without a separate edge-object store.

**Mechanic: cheaper logistics, not adjacency.** Ben's framing: 'logistics is always point-based — even if it can multiply, it has to cross a tile.' The existing road/logistics traversal cost is per-tile (the `road_level` tier curve, SUPPLY.md). A tile that **borders a river edge** gets a cheaper traversal weight on top of that curve — riverside tiles are cheaper to move goods across, stacking with (not replacing) the road-tier discount, mirroring the structural slot road tiers already occupy. This **replaces** the round-1 framing where a river only granted water-adjacency for farming — the primary mechanic is now logistics, though the water-adjacency read for [[BL-166]]/[[BL-168]]-style farming still holds as a secondary consequence (a tile bordering a river is also water-adjacent).

**Direction is mechanical.** Upstream/downstream is tracked per edge and **changes the traversal cost asymmetrically** — downstream crossing is cheaper than upstream, the same shape as the road tier's directionless-but-tiered discount, just now direction-sensitive. Rendering the direction (open art call, Ben's for now): propose a **shade gradient** — darker blue upstream, lighter/brighter blue downstream — as the simplest reading with no new glyph, consistent with existing terrain-tint rendering; a firmer call belongs to whoever builds the render pass.

**Not a resource.** Still no distinct freshwater good seeded — the mechanic is entirely the logistics discount (+ the water-adjacency side-effect), no new market good.

**Determinism.** Unchanged — the edge trace is still a deterministic function of the seeded height field (standing rule).

**Authority.** TILE_GENERATION.md for the edge-trace generation pass; SUPPLY.md gains the river discount alongside the road-tier table once landed (stacking rule lives there).

items.title: Budget ledger redesign — profit chart, stubbed policy levers, building-rank placeholder (Ben mockup)
items.summary: Filed + landed 2026-07-11 (Ben mockup). Redesigned the Budget (Balance) ledger from the itemised cashflow table to a mockup layout: corp-name header, a profit line chart (income − expenditure per econ tick), stubbed Tax/Wages tier controls, an Assets summary (buildings owned / income / cargo value), and a placeholder top-buildings-by-profit rank table. UI-only; the Tax/Wages mechanics are owed to BL-155.
items.design: **Landed 2026-07-11 (Ben's Budget-ledger mockup).** `draw_balance_ledger` (`src/ui/balance_ledger.cpp`) is rebuilt to Ben's vertical mockup: (1) a centred **corp-name** header; (2) a **profit line chart** — profit per econ tick = income − expenditure over the recent window, a gold polyline with a zero baseline (handles the early-game net loss, [[BL-112]]); this **replaces** the former itemised cashflow table ([[BL-072]]) here — Ben's call, 'too much detail at first glance', to reappear in a dedicated breakdown menu later; (3) stubbed **Taxes** and **Wages** tier controls ('– I II III IV V +', active tier green) — drawn and selectable (ui_state.budget_tax_tier / budget_wage_tier) but with **no economic effect**; their mechanics — Tax as a player-set policy lever, Wages as a cost↔workforce trade-off — are owed to [[BL-155]]; (4) an **Assets** summary — Buildings Owned, Income (economy report), Cargo Value (the shared `player_stockpile_value`, now exported from header_panel for reuse); (5) a **top-8 buildings-by-profit** table with a rank-change-vs-a-year-ago column — per-building net via [[BL-074]] (`rank_player_buildings_by_profit`), rank change compares the current rank to the ranking 4 econ ticks ago, which app snapshots each tick (`m_building_rank_hist`, ASCII +N/-N/= since the default font lacks arrow glyphs). Also fixed two bugs surfaced in review: the two tier controls' buttons collided on ImGui id (PushID per control), and a new selection while a ledger was open double-drew both for one frame (the new-selection close now runs before the ledgers draw). Verified via `scripts/verify/balance_ledger.lua` (empty-state) + `scripts/verify/budget_ledger_ranked.lua` (populated, builds producing sites). Residue: wire the Tax/Wages levers to real economics (→ [[BL-155]]); real building art (placeholders today).

items.title: Road tier ladder (Track/Road/Highway) + spanning/symmetric road render
items.completion_note: Landed 2026-07-11 (Ben). Two coupled fixes on the road render/economy path. (1) SPAN/SYMMETRY: body_surface_canvas.cpp road block rewritten — each roaded tile draws its own half of every shared edge (centre -> hex-edge midpoint) toward each roaded, survey-revealed cardinal neighbour (the 4 the intra-body A* traverses), so two roaded tiles meet at the midpoint as one continuous span with no 'from vs to' asymmetry; a centre cap keeps a lone/just-placed road visible; per-tile-tier styling. items.summary: Filed + built 2026-07-11 (Ben). Two coupled road fixes on the same render/economy path. (1) VISUAL SPAN FIX — the road render ([[BL-147]] ROAD_RENDER_PLACEMENT) drew a centre-to-centre segment only when BOTH a tile and its right/down cardinal neighbour carried a road, over a rectangular offset subset of the true hex adjacency; so diagonal roads read patchy and a segment 'belonged' to a pair, not a tile ('a road from ≠ a road to'). Rewritten so each roaded tile draws its OWN half-edge (centre → shared-hex-edge midpoint) toward every roaded, revealed, land hex-neighbour (all 6): two roaded tiles meet exactly at the edge midpoint = one continuous span, identical whichever tile is 'from'. Render-only — road_level stays a per-tile field (no save-format change). (2) TIER LADDER — the two generated tiers (local/trunk) become a named 3-tier ladder Track(1)/Road(2)/Highway(3), each a distinct cost-discount (road_traversal_multiplier 0.67/0.50/0.40) AND a distinct on-canvas weight/brightness; generation assigns by centre scale, the player places any tier from the build front door (upgrade-in-place allowed). Railroad is a separate transport MODE, not a road tier → [[BL-173]].
items.design:
**Built 2026-07-11 (Ben: 3-tier ladder, ship end-to-end; railroad → [[BL-173]]). Full-mode, main-session-serial** (the pieces are interdependent — the registry struct change ripples to placement + the build front door — so fan-out buys nothing).

**A. Render span/symmetry fix** (`body_surface_canvas.cpp`, the wrap-copy road block). Replace the right/down rectangular offsets + 'both ends roaded, drawn once' scheme with: for each roaded tile, iterate all 6 odd-r hex neighbours (the even_off/odd_off tables the Country-lens border pass already uses); for each neighbour that is roaded, survey-revealed and land, draw a line from this tile's screen centre to the MIDPOINT of the centre-to-neighbour-centre line, styled by THIS tile's tier. Each tile owns its half, so the two halves meet at the shared-edge midpoint (continuous, symmetric) and the survey fog clips cleanly at the boundary. Cylinder-seam wrap handled per neighbour (shift the neighbour screen-x by ±period when the raw column crossed the seam). The 4-cardinal logistics path is a subset of the 6 hex neighbours, so every generated/placed road edge is now drawn.

**B. Tier ladder.** road_level values: 1=Track, 2=Road, 3=Highway. `road_traversal_multiplier` (logistics.cpp) is unchanged — the existing 1/(1+0.5·tier) curve already yields 0.67/0.50/0.40 for the three tiers (diminishing returns). NOTE: roads model cost-discount, not a throughput cap (per-node capacity is out of prototype scope, SUPPLY.md) — 'lower throughput' = lower tier = less discount.

**C. Generation** (`road_generation.cpp`). Rename constants kLocal/kTrunk → kTrack(1)/kRoad(2)/kHighway(3); add kMidScale=2. Edge tier by the two centres' scales: both major (scale≥kMajorScale=3, City/Metropolis) → Highway; at least one Town+ (scale≥2) → Road; else → Track. Cross-nation border links stay Track (lowest). Deterministic (pure over scales/tiles); the astar_cost_cache clear at the end is unchanged.

**D. Economy/registry** (`recipe_registry.{hpp,cpp}`, `economy.lua`). `road_economics` (flat credits + per-resource materials) is unchanged as a struct; the registry now holds a `std::array<road_economics,3>` (Track/Road/Highway) and `road_econ(tier)` returns the tier's cost. Lua `economy.roads` becomes `track/road/highway` sub-tables; the loader reads all three. Defaults (also used by the Lua-free harnesses): Track 25cr/3 steel, Road 45cr/6, Highway 90cr/14.

**E. Placement** (`placement_rules.{hpp,cpp}`, `construction.{hpp,cpp}`). `place_road(w, reg, corp, tile, tier=1)` and `can_place_road(tc, tier=1)`. Upgrade-in-place: valid when non-ocean AND tile.road_level < tier (so you can raise a Track to a Highway but not re-lay the same/lower tier — `already_road` now means 'already at or above this tier'). Cost = the chosen tier's `road_econ(tier)`. Sets road_level=tier, clears astar_cost_cache (unchanged contract). The tier default 1 keeps every existing caller behaviour-identical.

**F. UI plumbing** (`ui_state.hpp`, `app.cpp`, `selection_panel.cpp`). `construction.pending_road_tile` gains a companion `pending_road_tier`; the build front door lists three road affordances (Track/Road/Highway), each with its own cost line + validity (greyed when tile.road_level ≥ tier or unaffordable); app passes the tier to place_road.

**G. Tools stay green.** `road_generation_harness.cpp` R2: assert Track+Road+Highway all present and the ceiling is road_level≤3 (was ≤2). `logistics_harness.cpp` T10: place Track (tier 1), expect the new Track default cost, and add an upgrade-succeeds / same-tier-rejected pair. Visual `roads.lua` extended to show the 3 tiers + the 3 front-door affordances.

**Authority:** SUPPLY.md (tier ladder + multipliers + generation mapping + placement) and GLOSSARY.md (Track/Road/Highway terms); PLANETARY.md/ICONS.md render note (spanning + 3 weights).

items.title: Railroad — a distinct land transport mode (rail lattice + rolling stock)
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-11 (Ben, road-fix thread). Railroad as a transport MODE distinct from the road tiers ([[BL-172]] made Track/Road/Highway cost-discounts on the shared land mode). Rail is not just a cheaper road: it wants its own network (tracks are placed, not a per-tile discount over open land), its own cost/speed profile, and plausibly its own gate (a rail depot at each end, like Port gates Sea). Design-owed.
items.design: **Idea — design owed.** [[BL-172]] settled that Track/Road/Highway are three tiers of the *land* mode (cost-discounts on the A* traversal of otherwise-open land). Railroad is qualitatively different and was deliberately deferred there: a rail line is its OWN network — you travel along laid track, not cheaply across open ground — with a distinct cost/speed profile (very low per-unit cost, high fixed build, bulk-favouring). Open questions to resolve at design: (1) Is rail a new `convoy.mode` value (SUPPLY.md's {land,sea,air,space} → +rail) with its own `base_logistics_cost`, or a fourth road tier with a connectivity constraint? Leaning: a real mode, because rail needs endpoint gating and can't reuse the 'cheaper open-land' model. (2) Gate — a **rail depot / station** building at both endpoints (mirrors Sea's Port gate, SUPPLY.md Infrastructure gates), Era 0. (3) Network model — a separate rail_level tile field + a placement affordance, pathing that can ONLY traverse rail tiles between depots (a hard network, not a discount). (4) Generation — do nations ship with an inter-city rail backbone, or is rail wholly player-built? (5) Render — a distinct glyph (cross-tie hatching) vs the road spans; ICONS/PLANETARY. Mechanically justified via Trade (bulk-freight arbitrage the road tiers can't make marginal). Deterministic (standing rule). **post-v0.1.0** — beyond the prototype's remaining arc; revisit once the road tiers + supply loop are proven in play. Authority → SUPPLY.md when designed. Ben road-fix thread 2026-07-11.

items.title: Orient legibility — a legible first move on load + nav-rail icon read
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-11 from the BL-098 legibility walkthrough (US-001, scored 2.5/5 — the lowest, jointly). Identity reads clearly on load (emblem + corp name + parent), but two orient-time gaps remain: the opening view suggests no first move, and the left nav-rail icons read as blank in every capture. Highest-leverage 'why it's hard for a human to sit down and play' finding. Design-owed — Ben to settle the cues.
items.design:
**Friction (BL-098 walkthrough, US-001).** The single biggest onboarding blocker set. Two strands:

**1. Nav-rail icon legibility.** In *every* walkthrough capture ~8 of the 11 left-rail slots render as empty squares — only the economy/bar-chart glyph and the top dot draw. A new player cannot tell what any menu does. **First: confirm whether this is genuine or a render artifact** — the rail affordances are hand-drawn vector strokes (ui::icons, ICONS.md); the captures ran through the software renderer, which *can* under-draw thin lines. If it reproduces in the interactive GPU build, give each rail slot a legible glyph + a hover tooltip/label (the ICONS.md vocabulary is the source of truth). If it's software-renderer-only, no code change — just note it.

**2. A legible first move.** US-001's weak half: the launch view frames who/where but suggests nothing to *do*. Options for Ben (pick one): a dismissible 'first move' hint; a highlighted starter action on the home-HQ Selection ('Construct Buildings'); or a one-line objective in the header/profile. Ties the 'what next' gap the story already flags.

**Evidence:** screenshots/walk_01_launch, walk_02_corp_lens (nav rail blank across both; no call-to-action). **Version provisional** — fits v0.1.0's legibility-polish theme; Ben re-slots. Traces US-001; parent review [[BL-098]]. Authority → LAYOUT.md (shell/rail) + ICONS.md (glyphs) when it lands.

- **Full (gated):** directional flow bound to actual persistent trade routes ([[BL-088]]) + per-unit *landed cost* visible at decision time (the US-009 friction), when the Layer-5 supply-route render lands. The solar route line ([[BL-039]]/[[BL-038]] substrate) is the legible half to build from.
