items.title: Workforce auto-solver - maximise-profit labour with the target as an editable heuristic
items.summary: Split from the 2026-07-15 building-management redesign. The UI shell (title/image, glyph-tagged production-method dropdown, profit + workforce graphs, and a 0-100 workforce-target button grid) landed on that session as the Buildings-tab detail (construction_panel.cpp draw_selected_section). THIS item is the deferred economy half: the player building's workforce should be AUTO-calculated each econ tick to maximise the building's net profit, with the workforce target reframed as an auto-computed heuristic the player may override, NOT an explicit goal.
items.design:
**Why:** Ben's steer - a manual workforce percentage is busywork; the interesting decision is the override, not the dial. The solver should land the workforce where marginal wage = marginal margin, then surface that as the default target the player can nudge.

**The load-bearing tension (design first):** the standing rule is *the player's own corp is never auto-acted on* (io-standing-rules.md; the BL-079 exception is background corps only). Auto-solving the player's workforce brushes that rule, so this needs an explicit reconciliation: is the solver an advisory *default* the player accepts/overrides (keeps agency, likely fine) or a silent per-tick mutation of the player's building (violates the rule)? Recommended framing: the solver computes a *suggested* target; the player's explicit override pins it until cleared. Determinism must hold (no float drift across save/load).

**Also owed (real data behind the shell):** per-building profit + workforce **history series** to replace the placeholder graphs, and proper per-method **glyphs** in ui::icons (the shell reuses the output resource pip). See the building-management shell notes in the same session's DEVLOG entry.

**Files:** economy_system.cpp (the solver, tick-gated), construction_panel.cpp (target buttons read the solved default), plus ICONS/PRODUCTION doc updates on landing.
items.resolution: Delivered (2026-07-15; status reconciled 2026-07-26). solve_workforce_target lands the per-tick profit-maximising workforce solver in economy_system.cpp, opt-out per building via building_component.workforce_auto (a manual target in the management UI pins it). The standing-rule reconciliation is recorded in .claude/rules/io-standing-rules.md (player-corp exception: this one dial only). Backlog status had not been flipped at landing - reconciled during the 2026-07-26 AI design session, which also names this solver as the set_workforce primitive AI corps reuse (AI_OPPONENT.md §5).

items.title: Corporate borders - HQ-projected influence range and the tall/wide specialisation axis
items.summary: Ben's steer (2026-07-18): corporations should have BORDERS like nations do - a corporate sphere projected outward from HQ building(s) with a RANGE, generalising the player-only home-ring/HQ-star chrome (BL-085) into a real ranged border for every corp on the Corporation lens. A corp opens with ONE HQ and builds more as it advances (tech/laws), which creates a TALL (deepen fewer HQs) vs WIDE (spread more HQs) specialisation axis. A gameplay mechanic - HQ range gates/modifies where the corp can operate - not just a visual layer. Deferred with corporation-system behaviour (post-v0.1.0); captured so the data model + lens rendering position for it.
items.design:
**Why (Ben's steer, 2026-07-18):** nations have real territory (Country lens: tile ownership + borders) but corporations only get tile *tints* on the tiles they directly hold, plus the player-only home-ring/HQ-star chrome (BL-085). Corporations should have **borders too** - a corporate sphere projected outward from **HQ building(s)** with a **range**, symmetric with how nations hold territory.

**Core model.** Every corporation has at least one **HQ** building. Each HQ projects an **influence range** (a radius / cost-field over the tile grid); the **union of a corp's HQ ranges is its border** (its operating sphere). A corp opens with **one HQ**; as it advances it can **build additional HQs**, each extending reach.

**The tall/wide axis (the point).** This is the specialisation lever: **tall** = invest in fewer HQs, deepening range/potency in place; **wide** = build more HQs, spreading the footprint across more territory (and eventually more bodies). Neither is strictly better - the choice shapes the corp's strategic character. This is what the mechanic is *for*.

**A gameplay mechanic, not just a visual.** The border is load-bearing: HQ range **gates or modifies where the corp can operate** (build / extract / project logistics), so it competes spatially with rival corporations and overlays - does not replace - nation jurisdiction. The exact effect is open (see below).

**Extensible via laws + technology.** HQ **range**, the **max HQ count**, and HQ **potency** are all levers laws and tech can move - this is the framework the later Policy/Research systems build on to differentiate corporations. The advancement that unlocks the 2nd+ HQ is itself a tech/law gate.

**Relationship to existing work.** The player-only home-cluster ring + `icons::hq` star (BL-085; CANVASES/PLANETARY) is the *seed* of this - a per-body 'my region' chrome around the player's holdings. This item **generalises** it into a real, ranged border for **every** corporation, surfaced on the **Corporation** lens (LENSES.md - today the lens only tile-tints held tiles + draws a player border) with the `hq` glyph (ICONS.md) marking each HQ.

**Open questions (why this is design-owed, not designed):**
- **Range shape** - fixed radius, or a decaying cost-field like the nation Voronoi-BFS budget (NATION_GENERATION.md)? A cost-field composes better with terrain and reads as 'reach'.
- **What the border gates** - build-only? an extraction/logistics bonus inside it? a hard operate-boundary? This sets how much it constrains vs. flavours play.
- **Overlap rules** - corp spheres vs. nation territory (a corp operating in a foreign nation), and corp-vs-corp overlap (contested tiles).
- **Per-body vs. global** - one HQ per body projecting locally (matches BL-085's per-body chrome), or a home HQ + weaker branch offices elsewhere.
- **Discovery interaction** - the border read against competitor-visibility + the activity fog (DISCOVERY.md: rival buildings visible, internals private).
- **Advancement curve** - which tech/law unlocks each further HQ, and the cost of going wide vs. tall.

**Prototype scope.** Deferred (post-v0.1.0). Corporation behaviour is deferred from the prototype (io-standing-rules.md; nation behaviour parked BL-054), so this lands with the corporation-system work, not before. Captured now so the data model and the Corporation-lens rendering can position for it.

**Files (on landing):** src/world/corporation_generation.cpp (HQ designation + range), the placement/economy seam (operate-gate), src/ui/body_surface_canvas.cpp + ui_state overlay (border render, generalising the BL-085 chrome); docs CORPORATION_GENERATION.md / LENSES.md / GLOSSARY.md / ICONS.md on landing.

**Design resolved (Ben, 2026-07-23) - core settled; the six opens above are answered, two sub-threads stay deferred:**

1. **Range shape -> decaying cost-field.** Potency tapers with distance from HQ. Within the sphere it is a soft gradient; at the ~20% floor construction becomes *impossible* - a hard build-boundary at the edge over a soft potency gradient inside. Composes with terrain, reads as 'reach' (not a fixed radius).

2. **What the border gates -> industry build-validity.** A building is only placeable inside the corp's border. Open sub-question Ben flagged: rather than a hard *extraction* cut-off at the edge, let extraction *taper*. The land-grab risk this raises is NOT solved by the taper but by the origin gate (#3).

3. **Origin gate (new - the anti-land-grab mechanic).** Corporations begin as **national** companies, confined to their home nation's territory. **International** operation is reserved for **1-2 great powers**, tech-gated. This steers the early game away from a 'who clicks the good tile first' free-for-all and gives the tall/wide axis room to grow into. Connects to CORPORATION_GENERATION.md's franchising / nation-seeded-privatisation / Era-sovereignty open items.

4. **Overlap -> tiles belong to both.** No exclusive ownership: a tile can carry a corp border AND nation territory at once. The active lens decides what is drawn - corp border in the corp's identity colour (Corporation lens), nation border in the national colour (Country lens). Because each tile holds only one building, there is **no competition for owned tiles**, so no contested-tile arbitration is needed.

5. **Per-body / structure -> single home HQ + weaker branch offices.** The exact potency of branches vs. the home HQ is a **calibration** left until multiplayer playtest begins.

6. **Discovery -> border implies vision.** Fog and border are mutually exclusive: a corp's border is itself a **vision source**, so it is impossible to have fog inside your own border.

**Deferred sub-threads (captured, not designed):**
- **Tech/law advancement curve** - which unlock gates each further HQ and the international-reach gate, plus the range / potency / max-HQ-count levers. Deferred with the Policy/Research systems.
- **Distance-based logistics bonus** - a proximity advantage (e.g. a steel mill sited near a feeding tile gets a logistics edge). Requires a **tile-to-tile nearness map** - infrastructure worth building regardless; this is one consumer of it. Parked until that map exists.

items.title: Corporate reach layer (visual slice of BL-182) - rival HQ border rings on the Corporation lens
items.summary: The in-scope, render-only first slice of BL-182: under the Corporation lens, each RIVAL corporation on the active body draws an HQ-projected border - a reach ring centred on its HQ (the holding nearest its holdings centroid) plus an hq star, in the corp's identity colour, radius = holdings extent + a fixed projected range. Extends the always-on player-only home ring/HQ star (BL-085) to rivals so corporations read as having borders too. The player's own border stays the BL-085 home ring (excluded here to avoid a double-draw). Gates nothing, mutates no state - the gameplay mechanic stays deferred in BL-182.
items.design:
**Slice, not the mechanic.** This ships only the *legibility* half of BL-182 (which stays parked for the full gameplay mechanic). Render-only; no operate-gating, no multi-HQ, no tall/wide, no law/tech levers.

**Implementation.** New block in body_surface_canvas.cpp immediately after the BL-085 home-presence block, gated on `state.overlay == overlay_mode::corporation`. Groups the active body's `tile_to_corp` tiles by owner (skipping the player), computes each corp's centroid, picks the HQ = nearest holding to the centroid, and draws a reach ring (radius = max HQ-to-holding distance + hex_size * 2.5, in the corp identity colour at ~59% alpha) plus an `icons::hq` star, cylinder-seam-wrapped like the BL-085 block.

**Why skip the player.** The always-on BL-085 home ring/HQ star already IS the player's border; drawing the reach layer for the player too would stack two rings + two identical HQ stars. Per LENSES.md the Corporation lens 'extends the identity language to rivals' - so the reach layer covers rivals and the player keeps its home ring.

**Verification.** `scripts/verify/corporate_reach.lua` (wide multi-corp view + player-HQ frame). Static cold review PASSED (compiles-by-inspection, standing invariants, geometry). NOTE: the full build + visual-verify could NOT be run in-session - the SDL3 FetchContent download is blocked by egress policy (403), and CI (build.yml) does not run the visual-verify tier (deferred, BL-057). items.title: Road-tier legend — teach the Track/Road/Highway read on the Planetary canvas
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-19 (design session, Ben) from the deferral explicitly noted at the BL-172 road-tier landing (DEVLOG 2026-07-11): the always-on road layer encodes Track/Road/Highway by thickness + brightness only (SUPPLY.md's three-tier ladder), with no legend or key anywhere in the UI, so the distinction is illegible to a new player. Settled 2026-07-19: contextual read on the tile Selection panel / hover tooltip, not a persistent chip.
items.design:
**Problem.** `body_surface_canvas.cpp`'s always-on road-edge pass renders three tiers (Track/Road/Highway = `road_level` 1/2/3) purely by line weight and brightness (thin+dim to thick+bright, per SUPPLY.md's ladder). There is no legend anywhere naming which is which, and roads are the only always-on canvas layer with a visual code and no key.

**Why it isn't a trivial drop-in.** Roads are deliberately NOT lens-gated - they render always-on like terrain (Ben's call at BL-147 landing), which is exactly why they were left out of the per-lens legend drawer (BL-164's fold-out legend is keyed to `overlay_mode`, so it only shows when a lens is active). Giving roads a legend means picking a home that doesn't imply 'roads are a lens.'

**Options considered:**
1. **Persistent chip** near the minimap/lens strip, always visible regardless of active lens - three swatches + tier name. Simplest to discover, but adds permanent chrome to an already dense corner (the same crowding concern that deferred this at BL-147/172 landing).
2. **Contextual read** in the Selection panel / hover tooltip when a road tile is hovered or selected - zero permanent chrome cost.
3. **One-time teach** - a dismissible callout the first time the player places or reveals a road, then never again. Teaches once, costs nothing after.

**Determinism/save.** Pure UI/render - no save-format or world-state change.

**Authority.** PLANETARY.md's road-render section already documents the tier ladder's visual encoding; this item adds the legend/teaching mechanism there once landed.

### Settled 2026-07-19 (Ben)
**Option 2 - contextual.** When a road tile is hovered or selected, name the tier ("Highway" etc.) and its traversal discount in the existing per-tile read surface - `draw_tile_selection` (`selection_panel.cpp`, the BL-162-adjacent tile mockup work) for the click path, and the existing hover tooltip in `body_surface_canvas.cpp` for the hover path. No new persistent chrome, no new file. Options 1 and 3 dropped.

items.title: Road ↔ commercial-reach fog interaction — should roads dim with tile vision?
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-19 (design session, Ben) from the deferral explicitly noted at the BL-147 road-render landing (DEVLOG 2026-07-10): roads draw full-bright on any survey-revealed tile, including ones the intra-body commercial-reach fog (BL-151/152) would otherwise dim under its analytic wash. Settled 2026-07-19: dim roads by tile vision, same as the lens fill.
items.design:
**Current behaviour.** The Planetary canvas's intra-body reach fog (DISCOVERY.md) derives a per-tile `vision` scalar each frame (1 in the permanent layers - own buildings, the corp-centre-to-market corridor - else the moving convoy beam's intensity); the fog wash applies `(1 - vision)` **over the lens fill**, so a fogged tile's analytic read dims with it. The road-edge pass in `body_surface_canvas.cpp` draws independently of that wash, so a road on a `vision ≈ 0` tile still renders at full brightness - identical treatment to a road on a tile the player actively operates.

**Is this actually wrong?** DISCOVERY.md is explicit that 'Survey owns the unrevealed tiles' and the reach fog's semantics are deliberately 'commercial reach, not unknown terrain' (Ben's call at BL-151 landing) - the home planet is the player's own soil, fog means *where your logistics operate*, not *where the land is unmapped*. A road is arguably physical infrastructure like the tile hex itself (visible once surveyed, never re-hidden), not activity knowledge - in which case full-bright-once-surveyed is correct and the DEVLOG deferral was a false alarm.

**The other reading.** The reach fog's whole point is to make the player's own commercial footprint pop (BL-154: 'your trade spine is always lit'). A road you've never trafficked competes visually with the corridors you actively use; dimming untouched roads the same as the lens fill would sharpen that contrast rather than contradict the fog's intent.

**Options considered:**
1. **Leave as-is** - roads are physical terrain, not activity; close this out by adding a line to DISCOVERY.md/PLANETARY.md stating the exclusion is deliberate, so the deferral doesn't resurface as a phantom bug.
2. **Dim roads by `(1 - vision)`** the same alpha multiply the lens fill already receives, reusing the per-tile `vision` value `body_surface_canvas.cpp` already computes - one multiply in the road draw pass, no new state.

**Determinism/save.** `vision` is already frame-derived, non-serialised VIEW state per DISCOVERY.md's stated invariant (never fed back into `world/*`) - either option is a pure render change.

### Settled 2026-07-19 (Ben)
**Option 2 - dim by vision.** Apply the same `(1 - vision)` alpha multiply the lens fill already receives to the road segment's draw colour in the road-edge pass (`body_surface_canvas.cpp`), reusing the existing per-tile `vision` value - no new state. DISCOVERY.md gains a line noting roads participate in the reach-fog wash like the lens fill, closing the physical-vs-activity ambiguity in favour of 'your own footprint outranks infrastructure you don't use.'

items.title: Laws ledger — the player-facing surface for enacting/repealing laws (BL-155 companion)
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-19 (design session, Ben) as the UI companion BL-155 explicitly excludes from its own scope ('no UI... committed - the point is to position the model'). BL-155's design is unusually settled for design-owed - a four-family effect taxonomy and ten named laws already enumerated - but nothing yet names how the player actually SEES or ENACTS a law. Settled 2026-07-19: Budget ledger keeps its own Tax/Wages controls; the Laws ledger shows those two laws read-only alongside the other eight.
items.design:
**Gap.** BL-155 (v0.1.2, Laws & policy surface) settles the law object shape - `condition_set` + polymorphic `effect`, four effect families (margin modifiers, quantity clamps, cost adders, gates), ten named laws, and the determinism seam (`run_economy_step` resolves all active laws' condition-sets at one fixed point) - but is explicitly data-model + stub only, no UI. This item is the missing player-facing half: a place to browse the law list, read what's active, and enact/repeal.

**Shape (matches the existing ledger family).** A new ledger window (`draw_laws_ledger`, alongside `balance_ledger.cpp` / the Market and Construction ledgers), nav-rail toggle per the standing Toggle rule (io-standing-rules.md - re-clicking the active nav icon closes it, doesn't collapse to an overview). Lists the ten BL-155 laws grouped by effect family, each row showing: name, one-line effect description, active/inactive state, and - for conditional laws - the `condition_set` gate in plain language (e.g. a wartime tax reads 'active only during war'). An enact/repeal control per law, gated on the player being able to afford/qualify (exact gate is BL-155's to define; this item only renders + dispatches the toggle).

**The BL-171 reconciliation (settled below).** The Budget ledger already carries stubbed **Tax** and **Wages** tier selectors (`ui_state.budget_tax_tier` / `budget_wage_tier`, drawn, no economic effect) built ahead of BL-155 landing. Two of BL-155's ten laws - **extraction tax** and **labour-contract floor** - are exactly what those stubs anticipate.

**Determinism.** Read-only + a single enact/repeal write per player action, landing on the same tick boundary BL-155's condition-set resolution already uses (laws read the *previous* tick's resolved values, never mid-tick mutating ones per BL-155's determinism seam) - this item adds no new determinism risk beyond what BL-155 itself introduces.

**Sequencing.** Hard-blocked on **BL-155** landing its data model and enforcement seam first - this item is the view over that model, not a parallel track. Natural to promote as the second half of the same v0.1.2 batch rather than a fully separate session.

### Settled 2026-07-19 (Ben)
**Stay separate.** The Budget ledger keeps its own simplified Tax/Wages tier selectors as the fast-path control (`ui_state.budget_tax_tier` / `budget_wage_tier`, wired to real economics once BL-155 lands - that wiring is BL-155's job, not this item's). The Laws ledger lists all ten laws for browsing, but shows **extraction tax** and **labour-contract floor** read-only there (state mirrors the Budget ledger's tiers; enact/repeal for those two happens on the Budget ledger, not here) - the other eight get full enact/repeal controls in the Laws ledger. Two surfaces, one law each is written from exactly one place, so no drift risk despite staying separate.

items.title: Food consumption model — plain market demand, no starvation mechanic
items.summary: Filed + settled 2026-07-21 (design session, Ben), closing an assumption this session's BL-166/168 design wrongly carried — that off-world/coastal food production needs a not-yet-built population consumer. Ben's call: population food demand is (and stays) a **plain market-demand pull**, never a starvation/health/death mechanic; Food rations arrive later as the tier-2 good the demand eventually targets.
items.design:
**Existing state (already live).** `run_economy_step` (`economy_system.cpp`, population-demand pass) already adds `pcc.scale` units of **agricultural_produce** demand per population centre into its body's market, every tick — this is a real, live market signal today, not a future dependency. Its own comment marks it a stub to be replaced by **food_rations** demand once the processing pipeline connects agricultural_produce → Food rations end-to-end (Food Processor recipe, RESOURCES.md), which is a separate, already-anticipated migration.

**Settled 2026-07-21 (Ben).** Population food demand is **permanently a plain economic pull** — it raises market demand for the good (agricultural_produce today, Food rations once the processing swap lands) and nothing else. There is **no starvation, health, or population-decline mechanic** tied to unmet food demand, now or later; an under-supplied market just clears at a higher price, same as any other scarce good (SCARCITY lens, MARKET.md pricing). This closes the open question POPULATION.md left implicit ('generates demand for food rations' didn't say what unmet demand *does*) and corrects this session's BL-166/168/170 design write-ups, which wrongly treated 'a food consumer' as not yet existing — it already does, via this stub, so [[BL-166]] (Hydroponics Bay) and [[BL-168]] (Fishing Wharf) have a real consumer for their output **today**, not only after a future population model lands.

**Follow-up (unscoped here).** The Food rations swap-in (agricultural_produce demand → food_rations demand, once Food Processor's recipe chain is wired to population) is the next real step Ben flagged ('we will use rations though later') — tracked as future work against this same authority doc, not filed as a separate item yet.

items.title: Endemic trade goods - the mercantile value track (C -> D)
items.summary: A fourth resource VALUE TRACK (mercantile) alongside industrial/ambient/habitability: endemic goods whose value comes from geography rather than utility. Generated by the biosphere in a new C -> D chain stage, bound to a latitude band AND a longitude sector, and priced per-market by distance from where they grow. Landed 2026-07-22.
items.design:
**Ben's ask (2026-07-22):** "Currently markets trade the same essential goods for space travel. Let's also insert C -> D. Before civilisation, resources such as tobacco should be generated, giving essential profit margins for trading based on geopolitical distance."

**The mechanic.** This is the same joint as B -> C on a different axis. B -> C asks what a world can BUILD with; C -> D asks what it is worth CARRYING FROM.

| | Made by | Value comes from |
|---|---|---|
| B -> C | the biosphere | **utility** - coal burns, iron bears load |
| C -> D | the biosphere | **scarcity by geography** - it only grows THERE |

Endemism is the real mechanism, and it is real history: nutmeg (Banda Islands), cinchona (Andes), tobacco (Americas) were worth crossing oceans for not because they were useful like iron but because you could not grow them at home.

**The problem it solves.** Every market previously traded the same industrial goods, so there was no structural reason to trade BETWEEN markets - only local shortage. Endemic goods create trade that exists because of where things are.

**Four goods, one per climate band:** tobacco (temperate/subtropical grassland), spices (tropical wetland/forest), coffee (subtropical forest), furs (subpolar/polar tundra). resource_count 19 -> 23. Safe to insert mid-enum: Lua binds resources by NAME through recipe_registry's lookup table, not by index, and no serialiser exists yet.

**Generation.** A new stage in run_planetology, gated on `life_stage >= land` - so the C -> D stage sits downstream of B -> C and a world with no forests has no cash crops either. Each good rolls whether this biosphere produced it at all (~60-70% each, mean 2.65 of 4 per world), then gets a latitude band (fixed per good) AND a longitude sector + width (rolled). The SECTOR is what makes it endemic rather than merely climatic: two worlds can both have temperate grassland and only one grow tobacco.

**Placement.** In tile_generation Pass 6, guarded by the planetology state. Unlike the BL-167 endowment - which SCALES an existing deposit - this ADDS one, because an endemic good has no base distribution to scale. A tile qualifies on band AND (wrapped) sector AND a composition the crop grows on; density falls off toward the sector edge so a region has a centre worth holding rather than a hard border.

**Pricing needed NO change to the clearing engine.** `market_component::base_price` is already per-market and authored at world creation, so an endemic good is simply cheap at its origin and dear far from it; supply/demand then push around that base as for any resource. `base_price = 1.5 x (1 + 7.0 x normalised_distance_to_nearest_source)`.

**Measured on a generated world:** tobacco 2.45 -> 8.19 (x3.34), spices 3.72 -> 7.56 (x2.03), coffee 1.84 -> 8.59 (**x4.67**). At the far end these beat steel (8.0). **The scarcest good commands the widest margin, and that is emergent rather than authored** - coffee had 30 source tiles against tobacco's 179, so it is further from more markets. Nobody tuned that.

**Distance is PHYSICAL for now.** Ben's call: "Let's leave it as just distance now. The word geopolitical will carry a weight when we add diplomacy and basic AI behaviour." The multiplier gains a political term later rather than being replaced.

**Verification:** planetology_harness R9 (a land biosphere evolves them; sterile/airless/core-fragment bodies evolve none; every good occurs on SOME world but none on EVERY world, so scarcity is real; each is confined to one band and one sector) and R10 (against a fully built world: the trade margin exists, and an endemic good covers only a small share of the land).

**Surfaced** in the New World wizard's Inheritance round as its own chart plus a line per good naming the band and region it grows in - the band and region ARE the value, so they are stated rather than left implicit.

**Open / deferred:** no dedicated extraction building yet (they generate as tile deposits and are extracted by the existing path); the goods are Kepler-only because markets are Kepler-only in the prototype - the same code gives the large off-world premium once markets exist elsewhere, which is the Era-0-trade-pays-for-Era-1 hook.

items.title: Gameplay affordances that generation only sometimes produces (highways, player processing facility)
items.summary: Deferred. Two measured cases where world generation produces a gameplay-relevant affordance only in a minority of worlds: the highway road tier (~37% of worlds have none) and the player opening with a processing facility (~25% of seeds). Both are pre-existing generation behaviour, surfaced by BL-167 measurement, not caused by it. Question is whether such affordances should be guaranteed, made more likely, or designed around.
items.design:
**Deferred (parked, F).** Surfaced during BL-167/BL-191 (2026-07-22) but explicitly NOT caused by them — both are pre-existing behaviour of population/road/corporation generation that only became visible once the default world changed and the harnesses started measuring across seeds. Ben: "we can work on the third issue waiting for me if it is a problem later."

**The shared shape.** Generation produces a gameplay-relevant affordance only in a minority of worlds, and a check or a player flow quietly depends on it. Neither case is a bug in the generator; both are an unstated assumption about what every world provides.

**Case 1 — the highway road tier. ~37% of worlds have none.** `edge_tier` (road_generation.cpp) returns Highway only when BOTH endpoints of a road edge are scale >= 3 (City+). Population scale is drawn from a fixed weighted distribution (40/30/20/8/2 for scales 1-5, population_generation.cpp), so ~30% of centres are City+ — but whether any such PAIR ends up adjacent in the road graph is spatial luck. Measured: highways present on 3 of 8 seeds. This broke `road_generation_harness` R2, which asserted the tier existed in one specific world; the check now asserts the tier is REACHABLE across seeds instead (a fragile assertion made honest, not weakened — had no seed produced one it would still fail).

**Case 2 — the player's opening processing facility. ~25% of seeds.** `scripts/verify/recipe_workforce.lua` realises US-007 ("steer a building's recipe and workforce") and needs the player to own a `processing_facility`; corporation generation only gives them one on some seeds. Measured by planetology_harness R11: 3 of 12 seeds (0x3C6EF362, 0xB54CDA26, 0x538453D7). The script now pins a known-good seed via the new `verify.new_world(seed)` binding, and R11 guards that such seeds keep existing. But it means **three quarters of campaigns open with no building whose production the player can steer**, which is a core Layer-3/4 flow.

**The design question (not settled here).** For each affordance, one of:
  (a) **Guarantee it** — post-process generation to ensure at least one (e.g. promote a centre pair to City scale; ensure the player corp's opening holdings include a processor). Cheapest to reason about, but it is exactly the "forced" clamping Ben rejected for the homeworld in BL-167, so it needs the same scrutiny.
  (b) **Raise the probability** — retune the scale-weight distribution or the corp focus mix so the affordance is common without being certain. Keeps generation honest; needs measurement to pick a target rate.
  (c) **Design around it** — accept that some worlds have no highways and some players start with only extractors, and make that a legible starting condition rather than a missing feature. Most interesting, and consistent with the BL-167 position that failure is content — but the UI must then not present an empty flow as if it were broken.

**Method note.** Whichever is chosen, MEASURE FIRST (the BL-167 pattern): the sweep harness shape (`tools/verify/planetology_sweep.cpp`) is the model — report the rate, then decide the target, rather than tuning blind.

**Related:** BL-132 (population/market co-generation, which would move population placement and so change case 1's rate), CORPORATION_GENERATION.md § Pass 3 (the lean focus-coherent holdings that drive case 2), USER_STORIES.md US-007.

items.title: Building stacks on one tile: the richness-derived cap, shared output, and depletion
items.summary: Several buildings may stand on one tile, capped by the tile's resource richness. The cap's shape landed with the building Selection element (placement_rules::stack_capacity, enforced via slot_full) but its constant is a placeholder and the economics are unsettled: stacked extraction sites currently each draw full nominal output from one shared reserve, multiplying output and depletion with no diminishing return. Settle output-sharing, the richness curve, and stack depletion.
items.design:
**Settled 2026-07-26 (AI design session; drafted by Claude, ratified by Ben same day).** Answers to the three open questions:

1. **Diminishing per-site output, honest shared depletion.** Site k in a stack (stored order, oldest first) produces `base_rate x richness x workforce x d^(k-1)` with **d = 0.8**. Stacking pays sub-linearly (2 sites = 1.8x, 5 sites = 3.36x, never 5x) while each site draws real reserve for what it extracts - so a full stack drains the deposit faster than its output multiple, making stack-vs-spread a genuine trade-off against transport and land rather than a dominant strategy. No clamps, no fake caps: the curve is the economics.

2. **Capacity curve stays richness/50, min 1** (0-250 band -> 1-5 sites) - retained deliberately: with diminishing returns carrying the economics, the cap is a *legibility* bound (how many markers a tile can host), not the balance lever. k_richness_per_site is promoted from placeholder to settled constant; revisit only if the marginal-site curve proves mistuned in play.

3. **Depletion taper is computed against the stack's combined nominal.** Aggregate the per-tile (type, target) stack's nominal draw; every member sees the same taper band and exhausts together (today each site tapers against its own nominal, so stack members desynchronise). run_extraction gains a per-tile stack pre-pass; deterministic, stored-order.

4. **Non-extraction stacking stays capacity 1 in this item.** Whether processors stack on land/workforce/road-tier is a different question - deferred, noted in the item, not blocked on.

**AI relevance (why now).** The BL-202 siting scorer prices the marginal site: `value(site N+1) = base x d^N x margin` - the same curve that stops the AI (and the player) from mindlessly stacking the one best tile. **Authority** -> docs/economy/PRODUCTION.md (stacking is a production rule) on landing; placement_rules.cpp + economy_system.cpp (run_extraction stack pre-pass) + selection_panel.cpp readout.

items.design:

The convention was corrected forward but already-deleted rows were never restored, leaving live `requires` edges pointing at an id present in no item, archive, or commit oracle. The row is restored here so the dependency graph resolves and the 'Do not delete landed entries' convention holds retroactively. Commit fd97f81 (2026-07-23) subject: 'Sticky detail card: cursor-anchored frame, Selection content, drill-down, three-region tile card (BL-194/195/196/198)'.

items.title: Move the Selection element wholesale into the sticky card; column becomes ledgers-only

Explicitly a MOVE, not a redesign: whether BL-123's tile layout should be redrawn for the card is deferred to an either/or decision after Ben has played with the style. Frees the column to be ledgers-only.
items.design:
**Settled 2026-07-22 (design session, Ben).** The Selection info element moves **wholesale** out of the shell fold-out column and into the BL-194 card.

**Move, do not redesign.** Ben's explicit call: relocate the existing content as-is. Whether the BL-123 tile layout (placeholder image → `[x, y]` caption → per-resource Tile-vs-P10 graphs → 2×2 action grid) should then be **redrawn** for the card's proportions is deliberately deferred — "we will treat this as an either/or problem after I've had a chance to play with this style". Do not take that decision inside this item.

**Consequences.**

- The fold-out column becomes **ledgers-only**. The mutual-exclusion rule (SELECTION.md § Layout, LAYOUT.md § Selection info element) — a new selection closes any open ledger to claim the column, selection state persists behind an open ledger and reappears when it closes — is **deleted outright**, not reworked. Selection no longer competes for the column, so the whole dance disappears.
- The BL-124 `foldout_column_rect` sizing for the Selection panel goes away. The card sizes to its content, clamped to the canvas rect (BL-194).
- **BL-123 SELECTION_ELEMENT_RESIZE is superseded in motive** — it existed to re-lay-out the wide action|facts content for the *narrow column*. Once the element is out of the column that pressure is gone. Do not close BL-123 until the play-test either/or above is settled; re-scope it rather than delete it.
- The card becomes the house style for future tooltips and explainers (Ben, Q5).

**Docs.** SELECTION.md takes the major edit — the element relocates, and § Layout & chrome plus the BL-124 column-sidebar prose are superseded. LAYOUT.md § Selection info element and § Ledger windows both change. MENU.md's broad-vs-targeted rule still holds, but its "targeted → reached through the Selection info element" clause needs rewording to name the card. TOOLTIP.md becomes the card family's authority — note that it currently and wrongly states nothing is implemented, which is stale as of BL-060/BL-020.

**Backlog audit correction (2026-07-29).** The content-move landed in commit fd97f81 (2026-07-23), bundled with BL-194/196/198 under one commit. The card THAT content moved into was later retired by BL-213 (2026-07-28/29): the click-anchored card became a fixed bottom band. BL-195's intent — Selection out of the fold-out column, column becomes ledgers-only — stands as delivered; the mechanism is BL-213's band, not the original card. Marking complete rather than re-scoping: nothing in this item's remaining prose describes work still owed.

items.title: Recursive drill-down — elements inside a card open child cards, bounded by acyclicity
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-22 (design session, Ben). Elements inside a card are themselves clickable, opening a child card. Depth is bounded by ACYCLICITY (a path may not revisit an ancestor) rather than a fixed number, with a ~20-level hard cap purely as a backstop. Strict stack; siblings swap rather than stack; Esc unwinds one level.
items.design:
**Settled 2026-07-22 (design session, Ben).** Elements inside a card are themselves clickable and open a **child card** — the card is recursive.

**Depth is bounded by acyclicity, not a fixed number.** Ben's call: "we won't allow paths that are looping, otherwise it has to be explicit like 20 levels". Keep a breadcrumb of the ancestor `(kind, entity_id)` pairs currently on the stack. A candidate child already present in that breadcrumb is **not offered** — the affordance simply is not drawn. No dead link, no error dialog. An explicit hard cap (~20 levels) sits behind that purely as a runaway backstop.

**Stack semantics.** A strict stack. Clicking a **sibling** element **swaps** the current child rather than stacking a second card beside it — only one path is live at a time. `✕` and **Esc** unwind exactly **one** level; unwinding from the root closes the card entirely.

**Primitive.** Nested `ImGui::BeginPopup` provides the stack and its unwind ordering natively; `ImGui::BeginTooltip` provides neither (and accepts no input, per BL-194). This is the concrete reason the primitive choice matters, recorded here so it is not relitigated at implementation time.

**Content contract.** Child cards reuse the existing `draw_hover_content` dispatch (`src/ui/hover_content.hpp` — title + ≤2 stat lines + 1 why-line, keyed on entity kind × active lens) rather than growing a parallel builder family. This is the same shared-builder seam TOOLTIP.md already designed for. An element with **no registered builder offers no drill-down** — that is how the recursive set stays bounded and implementable rather than "everything is clickable".

**Worked example (Ben, Q7).** From a tile card's Tile-vs-P10 resource graph, drilling into a resource opens a child card carrying the BL-197 chart: the body/world aggregate for that resource over time, with the tile's own series as a second line. The tile is an ancestor on that path, so the child card does not offer a drill-back into it.

**Backlog audit correction (2026-07-29).** Landed in commit fd97f81 (2026-07-23): `ui.card_stack` (`ui_state.hpp`) is the acyclic drill-frame stack, `selection_card.cpp`/`selection_panel.cpp` implement the push/swap/unwind semantics described above, explicitly commented `Recursive drill-down (BL-196)` in `selection_card.hpp`. Survived BL-213's card-to-band rename intact. Backlog status was never flipped at the time; corrected in this audit.
items.resolution: Delivered via fd97f81 (2026-07-23). Backlog status was never flipped at the time; corrected in this audit.

items.title: Chart container — titled, legended, dual-axis time-series element for cards and ledgers
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-22 (design session, Ben), specified from a Power BI reference screenshot. A reusable chart element the sticky card and any ledger can host: plain title, inline legend row, dual independent Y axes, hierarchical Year/Quarter X axis, optional log scale, hover crosshair. Carries one open call — hand-draw via ImDrawList vs adding ImPlot.
items.design:
**Settled 2026-07-22 from Ben's Power BI reference screenshot.** A reusable chart element the sticky card (BL-194/196) and any ledger can host. The reference shows, and the element must support:

- A plain left-aligned **panel title**, with an **inline legend row** immediately beneath it — a coloured dot plus series name per series.
- **Dual Y axes at independent scales**, each with its own axis label. The reference plots "Sum of World Iron" (bars, 0–100K, left axis) against "Sum of Tile Iron" (line, 50–100, right axis): the **aggregate is bars, the specific series is a line drawn over them**. That is exactly the aggregate-vs-tile comparison BL-198 feeds, and it is the reason dual axes are load-bearing rather than decorative — the two magnitudes differ by ~1000×.
- A **hierarchical time X axis** — Quarter grouped under Year. This maps directly onto the quarterly economy tick and the `1960 Q1` calendar (`src/core/sim_loop.hpp`), so the axis is the econ-tick axis.
- **Optional log scale** (the reference's second chart runs 100 / 1000 / 10000).
- A **hover crosshair** with a per-series marker at the hovered X.

**Do not copy from the reference:** its lower chart's X axis is out of chronological order (Q1 2001, Q1 2000, Q4 2001, Q4 2000 …) — a categorical-sort artifact of the source tool, not design intent. The axis is always chronological.

**Open call — the plotting substrate (Ben's).** ImGui ships only `PlotLines` / `PlotHistogram`: no dual axis, no legend, no log scale, no crosshair. Two routes:

(a) **Hand-draw via `ImDrawList`**, extending the precedent already set by BL-123's tile graphs (nice 1/2/5 axis-ceiling rounding, dotted gridlines, 0/ceiling/mid ticks) and the existing `PlotLines` call sites (`header_panel.cpp` sparkline, `construction_panel.cpp:332`). Matches the house style exactly; but dual-axis + log + crosshair + legend is a lot of chart code to own.

(b) **Add ImPlot**, which provides all five features natively, integrates with ImGui directly, and is MIT-licensed; but it is a new dependency and its default styling needs theming to match the shell.

Recommendation: **(b)** if the full dual-axis + log + crosshair set is genuinely wanted; **(a)** if the element can start as bars-plus-line on a single axis and grow. A dependency add touches `docs/tech/TECH_FOUNDATIONS.md`, so this is Ben's call and should be the **first task** of this item, not an implementation-time improvisation.

**Build it against existing data first.** `m_balance_history` / `m_income_history` / `m_expenditure_history` (`src/core/app.hpp:211`) already exist as capped ring buffers, so the element can be proven and captured before BL-198 lands any new series.

**Backlog audit correction (2026-07-29).** The open call was resolved for (a): commit 491d18a (2026-07-23) hand-draws `ui::charts::draw_time_series` via ImDrawList — dual Y axes, hierarchical Year/Quarter X axis, optional log scale, hover crosshair, house-style dotted gridlines/nice_ceil. Wired into the card the same session (fd97f81). Reused since (BL-211's `generation_charts.cpp` calls the same `charts.cpp` primitive) rather than duplicated. Backlog status was never flipped at the time; corrected in this audit.
items.resolution: Delivered via 491d18a (2026-07-23, the chart element) and fd97f81 (2026-07-23, wired into the card). ImDrawList hand-draw was chosen over adding ImPlot. Backlog status was never flipped at the time; corrected in this audit.

items.title: Resource time-series store — body aggregates always, per-tile series lazily on first drill-down
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-22 (design session, Ben). BL-197's headline chart needs per-body-per-resource and per-tile-per-resource time series, neither of which exists — the only history in the build is the three corp-level balance/income/expenditure ring buffers on `app`. Follows that precedent (app-owned, capped, unserialised, outside the save seam) and makes the per-tile series LAZY to contain data growth.
items.design:
**Settled 2026-07-22 (design session, Ben).** BL-197's headline chart — an aggregate resource series with the selected tile's own series drawn over it — needs two time series that **do not exist**. Confirmed by inspection: the only history in the build is `m_balance_history` / `m_income_history` / `m_expenditure_history`, app-owned capped ring buffers (`src/core/app.hpp:211`, fed by `ui::push_capped`), and they are **corp-level only**.

**Follow the existing precedent — app-owned, capped, unserialised.** Those three buffers live on `app`, not on `world`, so they sit **outside the save seam entirely**. Keeping the new series there too means **no save-format change and no determinism risk**: the history survives the session only. For a prototype analysis surface that is the right trade, and it keeps this item off the serialisation seam that would otherwise make it Full-mode-expensive.

**Per-tile must be lazy.** Bodies × resources × ticks is cheap and can be recorded unconditionally. Tiles × resources × ticks is **not** — a body carries thousands of tiles, and ROADMAP's v0.1.0 done-definition names data growth as an explicit cut criterion ("Performance and data growth hold"). So:

- **Body aggregates: recorded always**, one sample per economy tick, capped.
- **Per-tile series: recorded only from the first time the player drills into that tile.** A tile's line therefore *starts* at the moment of first inspection rather than at campaign epoch.

**Label the lazy start honestly.** A tile series that begins mid-chart must read as "recording began here", not as a resource that appeared from nothing. Do **not** back-fill or synthesise the missing prefix — an invented history in an analysis surface is worse than a short one.

**Open note — aggregate scope.** Ben's Q7 phrasing said "all of that resource on **body** vs time"; the Power BI reference is captioned "Sum of **World** Iron". Whether the aggregate series is body-scoped, world-scoped, or a selectable scope on the chart is unsettled. Surface it as a scope selector on the chart if the choice is cheap; otherwise default to body (the tile's own parent) as the more decision-relevant comparison.

**Backlog audit correction (2026-07-29).** Landed in commit fd97f81 (2026-07-23) as `m_body_resource_hist` (always) / `m_tile_resource_hist` (tracked tiles only, from first drill) on `app` (`src/core/app.hpp:228-229`) — app-owned, capped, unserialised, matching this design's precedent exactly. The aggregate-scope open note defaulted to body-scoped. Backlog status was never flipped at the time; corrected in this audit.
items.resolution: Delivered via fd97f81 (2026-07-23). Backlog status was never flipped at the time; corrected in this audit.

items.title: AI opponent — research + architecture proposal for a competent, human-skill computer player
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-23 (Ben, SSS). Ben's call: AI-opponent development can now proceed ALONGSIDE basic mechanics rather than waiting. This is the research + design spike that precedes any build: understand how Io actually plays, how grand-strategy-MP AI is normally built, and how to SIMPLIFY that into an opponent of roughly HUMAN skill (competent and beatable, not superhuman, not a handicapped pushover). The hardest part is a diverse spread of good training/evaluation data — but Io has infinite deterministic seeds to examine. First activity: review the current state of the art. Design/research only; does not implement AI behaviour (respects the standing rule until a real design lands).
items.design:
**Why now (Ben, 2026-07-23).** Until now the standing rule deferred AI faction behaviour beyond the data-model minimum stub (scoped exceptions: BL-079 local corp agency, BL-181 player workforce auto-solve). Ben has decided the AI OPPONENT thread can develop in parallel with the basic mechanics from here on. This item is the **research + architecture proposal** that must come before any build — it is design/research only and implements nothing, so it does not break the standing rule; the rule relaxes for real once this item produces an accepted design.

**The goal.** A computer opponent of **roughly human skill** — competent enough to be a genuine rival across Io's loop (resource extraction, trade, and — later — conflict), **beatable** by a decent human, and **legible** in its behaviour (its moves should read as sensible, not alien or obviously scripted). Explicitly NOT the goal: a superhuman optimiser, or a fake AI that only competes via economic handicaps.

**Three knowledge inputs the research must gather:**

1. **How Io actually plays.** The real decision surface a player faces — where to build (tile/terrain/deposit choice via placement_rules), what to produce (recipe selection, workforce dial), how to route supply (intra/inter-body logistics), how to trade (the order book, market clearing), and how corps win or die (the economy loop, debt, boom-bust). Grounded in the current code: `world/economy_system.cpp`, `market_clearing.cpp`, `construction.cpp`, `logistics.cpp`, `budget_system.cpp`. The AI plays the SAME game the player does, through the same seams.
2. **How grand-strategy / 4X multiplayer AI is normally built.** Survey the conventional toolkit: utility AI / scoring systems, GOAP, behaviour trees, HTN planners, hierarchical goal/agent decomposition (strategic → operational → tactical), scripted 'build orders' / opening books, and the standard difficulty levers (genuine skill vs resource handicaps vs information asymmetry). What Paradox / Civ / Stellaris-class titles actually ship, and their known failure modes (AI that can't play the economy, that cheats visibly, that stalls).
3. **How to SIMPLIFY to a similar-skill opponent.** Given Io's specialist-corp premise (lean actors on a saturated nation-owned substrate), the AI's decision space is narrower than a full 4X empire — lean into that. Identify the minimal competent policy: a small set of scored decisions (build/idle/switch-recipe/route/trade) that already exists as the BL-079 local-agency seam, escalated to strategic choices. The art is matching human skill, not maximising.

**The data problem — and Io's unfair advantage.** The hardest task in any learned or tuned AI is a **diverse spread of good data** (states, good moves, outcomes). Io's asset: **infinite deterministic seeds.** `make_hard_coded_world(seed)` yields unlimited, reproducible worlds; the sim is deterministic and headless-runnable (`--verify`, the `tools/verify/*` harnesses). That enables: seed-sweep scenario generation, self-play / bot-vs-bot rollouts, offline evaluation of a candidate policy across thousands of worlds, and regression-testing AI skill the same way we golden the UI. Any data strategy should exploit this rather than hand-authoring scenarios.

**State of the art to review FIRST (Ben's parenthetical).** Before proposing an architecture, review current SOTA and place Io within it: classical game AI (utility/GOAP/BT/HTN), grand-strategy AI post-mortems, and modern learning approaches — self-play RL (AlphaStar/OpenAI-Five lineage and why they are heavy), imitation/offline RL, and **LLM-driven agents** (where a structured, discrete, deterministic economic state like Io's is unusually amenable to an LLM or a hybrid LLM-planner-over-scored-primitives, and where it is not). Io is C++/Lua with a clean serialisable world model and a Lua scripting seam — note which approaches that architecture favours (e.g. an out-of-process policy over a compact state export vs an in-engine scored planner). **Claude should run this SOTA review** (the deep-research harness fits) as the item's opening activity.

**Deliverables of this item (research → design):**
- A short SOTA map placing Io's AI problem in the landscape, with the shortlist of viable approaches and their trade-offs for THIS codebase.
- A proposed **AI-opponent architecture** for Io: the decision decomposition, the seams it plugs into (extending the BL-079 agency seam vs a new planner), and the human-skill-calibration approach.
- A **data strategy** that exploits infinite seeds (generation, self-play, offline eval, skill-regression harness).
- A staged build plan (what lands first — likely a scored heuristic opponent over the existing seams — and what a learned layer would add later), written into `docs/ai/AI_OPPONENT.md` (new authority doc) and decomposed into follow-on backlog items.

**Scope guard.** This item produces research + a design + follow-on items. It does NOT implement AI behaviour; the standing-rule relaxation is earned only when the resulting design is accepted. Keep the first shippable increment small and legible (a scored heuristic over existing deterministic seams), consistent with Io's 'legible over clever' tone.

**SOTA research landed (2026-07-23):** the state-of-the-art review — this item's mandated opening activity — is written to docs/ai/AI_OPPONENT.md (SOTA map across the four areas, shortlist A-D, recommended staged path A->B = scored utility over the BL-079 seam then Victoria-3-style predictive-spending, data strategy exploiting infinite seeds, and an Io-specific verdict; 17 cited sources). Still owed before the standing-rule relaxation is earned: Ben's acceptance of the target architecture and decomposition into follow-on backlog items (AI_OPPONENT.md § 5). Item stays design-owed until then.

**Closed (2026-07-26).** Architecture accepted; decomposition + command seam + state-export schema + chat principle written to AI_OPPONENT.md §5-8; follow-on items BL-202..205 filed. The standing-rule relaxation is earned for the scoped path only (AI corps via corp_command; player corp untouched beyond the BL-181 dial).
items.resolution: Delivered (2026-07-26). Ben accepted the A->B utility-core architecture; the decision decomposition (candidate-action set, scoring terms, hysteresis/action budget, staggered cadence over the BL-079 seam), the corp_command seam + visibility-honest state-export schema (shared with multiplayer lockstep per MULTIPLAYER_PRINCIPLES.md), and the communication/diplomacy chat principle all landed in docs/ai/AI_OPPONENT.md §5-7. Decomposed into follow-ons: BL-202 (A scorer + command seam), BL-203 (B predictive spending), BL-204 (skill harness + state hash), BL-205 (corp chat log). Companion economics settled same session: BL-153, BL-193; BL-160/161 confirmed as AI trade primitives.

items.title: Dwell-to-open - holding the pointer still over an entity opens the sticky detail card
items.summary: The owed refinement to the sticky detail card (BL-194/196): the card gains a SECOND opener alongside the click. Holding the pointer STILL over an entity fills a small progress bar at the cursor; when it completes, the card opens on that entity - the pointer-driven twin of click-to-open. Ben's settled call (2026-07-23): a click STILL opens the card instantly; dwell is the additional hover opener, not a replacement. Anti-bombardment: the dwell timer advances only while the mouse holds still, so sweeping the pointer across the dense tile grid never auto-opens. The progress bar lives in the nested hover tooltip, not the card header. Scoped to the Planetary surface, where the hover infrastructure (hover_ticks + draw_hover_card) and the tile-density bombardment problem both live; click-to-open is unchanged on every canvas.
items.design:
**Settled (Ben, 2026-07-23).** The sticky card (BL-194) opens on a click. This adds a **second, pointer-driven opener**: hold the pointer still over an entity and a small **progress bar fills at the cursor**; on completion the card opens on that entity, exactly as a click there would.

**Click still opens instantly (Ben's explicit call).** Dwell is an *additional* opener, not the sole one. A left-click opens the card immediately as it always has; the dwell path is for the player who is reading the map with the pointer and wants the card without a click. The two paths converge on the same open (set `selected_entity`, clear `selection_hidden_for`, freeze `card_anchor` at the pointer).

**Anti-bombardment via stillness gating (the point).** The dwell timer advances only while the mouse is genuinely **still** - movement beyond a small jitter radius resets it. Sweeping the pointer across the dense tile grid therefore never trips an auto-open; only a deliberate hold does. This is why the trigger is stillness, not mere same-entity hover (which the transient glance already uses).

**Two timers, two jobs.** `hover_ticks` (entity stability - resets on entity change) governs the **transient glance** (the hover tooltip, unchanged, kHoverDelay). `dwell_ticks` (stillness - resets on movement) governs the **auto-open**. They run together when the pointer is held still, so the glance appears first and the bar then fills under continued stillness - natural progressive disclosure.

**The bar lives in the nested tooltip, not the card header (Ben's steer).** The fill indicator is rendered as a thin bar inside the transient hover tooltip at the cursor - the pre-open dwell indicator. A progress bar never belongs in the *opened* card's header. The bar shows only while dwelling (fraction strictly between 0 and 1); it vanishes the instant the card opens or the pointer moves.

**Scope: the Planetary surface only.** The hover infrastructure (`hover_ticks`, `draw_hover_card`) and the tile-density bombardment problem both live on `body_surface_canvas.cpp`; Solar/Circumplanetary use ad-hoc `SetTooltip` over sparse bodies where dwell-to-open earns little. Click-to-open is unchanged on all three canvases. Extending dwell to the other canvases is a cheap follow-up if wanted, but is deliberately out of this item.

**Suppressed in construction mode.** While a placement gesture is armed, a dwell must not retarget the Selection element - the same suppression the click path already applies.

**Tunables (flag for Ben's feel-check in play):** `kDwellOpenTicks` (frames of stillness to open, starting ~45-50 = ~0.8s at 60fps) and `kDwellJitterPx` (movement that resets the timer, ~4px). Both single constants in hover_card.hpp.

**Verification caveat.** The headless verify harness drives selection directly (`select_tile` / `dismiss_selection`) and has **no per-frame mouse/hover injection**, so the dwell path cannot be exercised by the existing sticky_card.lua. The state math is unit-reviewable and the click path is unchanged; live verification of the dwell feel is owed on a build-capable machine (same posture as BL-183). Extending the harness with a hold-mouse-still primitive is a possible follow-up.

**Backlog audit correction (2026-07-29).** Landed in commit d46e74f (2026-07-23, same session as BL-197/196/198). `hover_ticks`/`dwell_ticks` and the stillness-gated auto-open shipped as designed. BL-213 (2026-07-28/29) later removed this item's `card_anchor` writer as dead code when the click-anchored card was retired for a fixed band — the dwell TIMER logic is unaffected, only the now-pointless cursor-anchoring it used to set. Backlog status was never flipped at the time; corrected in this audit.
items.resolution: Delivered via d46e74f (2026-07-23). Its card_anchor writer was later removed as dead code by BL-213 (2026-07-28/29); the dwell-open mechanism itself is untouched. Backlog status was never flipped at the time; corrected in this audit.

items.title: Corporate border data-model foundation (slice of BL-182) - persisted HQ + influence range, border render off real data
items.summary: The in-scope, deterministic first slice of BL-182 (Ben's 2026-07-23 'Foundation only' call): give the corporate border a real data model instead of a render-time recompute. corporation_component gains a persisted HQ (the seat = holding nearest the holdings centroid on the home body) and an influence_range (holdings extent + a fixed projected reach, in unit-hex distance), both designated deterministically at generation. The Planetary border render (player home-ring BL-085 + rival reach rings BL-183) is unified onto a single lambda that reads this persisted data, drawn on each corp's home body. Gates nothing, mutates no sim state - the operate-gate gameplay mechanic stays deferred in BL-182 (post-v0.1.0).
items.design:
**Slice, not the mechanic (Ben, 2026-07-23 'Foundation only').** BL-182's full mechanic (operate-gating, national origin gate, tall/wide, law/tech levers) stays parked post-v0.1.0. This ships only the *data-model + render-off-real-data* foundation it needs, which is deterministic world-gen + a render swap - cleanly in prototype scope, no corporation behaviour.

**Data model (components.hpp).** `corporation_component` gains `entity_id hq_building` and `float influence_range`. The HQ is the corp's **seat** - the holding nearest its holdings centroid on the home body. The range is the furthest holding's distance from that HQ plus a **fixed projected reach** (2.5 units), all in **unit-hex distance** (hex_size = 1), so a renderer gets pixels by `influence_range * hex_size * zoom`, matching `ui::hex_local_centre`'s geometry exactly. A corp with no home-body holdings keeps `{null_entity, 0}` - no border.

**Generation (corporation_generation.cpp).** New anonymous-namespace helpers `hex_unit_centre` (mirrors the UI hex geometry, 2 lines, kept in the world layer to avoid a UI dependency) and `designate_hq`; wired into the assembly loop before `assets` is moved. Pure function of the placed holdings, so it adds no non-determinism.

**Render (body_surface_canvas.cpp).** The player home-ring (BL-085) and rival reach block (BL-183) each open-coded a render-time centroid+hull recompute; both are replaced by ONE `draw_corp_border` lambda reading the persisted seat + range, drawn on the corp's HOME body (single-home model; branch offices on other bodies deferred). Player border stays always-on identity chrome; rival borders show under the Corporation lens.

**Two deliberate foundation choices flagged for a play-test eyeball:** (1) the range is fixed at generation, so the player's ring no longer grows as they build outward (design-forward: the border is HQ-projected, not holdings-tracking); (2) a single projected-range constant now sizes both player and rival rings (was two ad-hoc render constants).

**Verification.** `tools/verify/world_audit.cpp` gains BL-182 R1 (every home-holding corp has a valid HQ that is one of its own buildings on the home body, plus a positive range) and R2 (HQ designation identical across two generations). Both PASS headlessly (8 corps, 0 bad, 0 non-deterministic); all pre-existing world_audit checks still PASS. The render is visual and could NOT be built in-session (SDL FetchContent egress 403 blocks the GUI build) - a rendered eyeball on the two flagged choices is owed on a build-capable machine. Also fixed a stale world_audit source list in tools/verify/README.md (missing city_names / planetology / road_generation / logistics TUs).

**Follow-ups fold back into BL-182:** the operate-gate, the national origin gate, branch offices on non-home bodies, the cost-field vs fixed-radius range shape, and the tall/wide advancement curve all remain in BL-182 (post-v0.1.0).

items.title: Corp AI stage A — scored utility layer over the agency seam, via the corp-command seam
items.summary: Stage A of the accepted AI architecture (BL-199, AI_OPPONENT.md §5-6): grow the BL-079 reflex block into a scored strategic layer. Each AI corp, on a staggered deterministic cadence, enumerates bounded candidates over the player-grade verb set (build / demolish / set_recipe / set_workforce via the BL-181 solver / idle / dispatch_convoy / place_road / survey), scores them with existing estimators (estimate_building_profit, placement affinities, live prices), applies hysteresis (do-nothing bias, cooldowns, streaks) and an action budget, and emits corp_command records applied at the tick boundary through player-grade validation - no bypass, no cheats. The command stream + score rationale is retained as the decision log (ring buffer): the AI legibility surface, the replay artifact, the BL-204 harness input, and the BL-205 chat feed. Includes the visibility-honest compact state export (JSON, versioned) for future out-of-process policies. Difficulty 5 - promote as multiple tasks (command seam; candidate enumeration; scorer; decision log/export).
items.design: The full decomposition lives in AI_OPPONENT.md §5 (cadence, verb table, scoring formula, hysteresis/budget, determinism rules) and §6 (corp_command seam, decision log, state-export schema) - accepted by Ben 2026-07-26. This item implements it. Scoped standing-rule relaxation: AI corps act strategically ONLY via this seam; the player corp is never auto-acted on beyond the BL-181 dial. Prices the BL-153 freight premium and BL-193 stack curve once those land (soft dependency - the scorer lands against current economics and re-weights; requires stays empty). BL-160/161 verbs activate when those items land.

items.title: Corp AI stage B — strategy layer, priority buckets, predictive spending (the solvency answer)
items.summary: Stage B of the accepted architecture (AI_OPPONENT.md §2B): the Victoria-3 import that makes the AI genuinely solvent instead of handed resources. Adds (1) a strategy layer - each AI corp holds a coarse strategy (extraction specialist / processing / trade arbitrage) derived from its generated industrial focus, biasing the BL-202 scorer; (2) priority buckets - Must-Have (wages, maintenance, debt service) > Should-Have (input feed for running processors) > Nice-to-Have (expansion), where a lower bucket may never starve a higher one; (3) predictive spending - before committing a build, forecast its market impact (post-completion supply delta vs current demand at the local market) so the AI does not over-build into its own glut. Replaces BL-202's crude reserve-floor solvency gate. Difficulty 4.
items.design: Genre post-mortem grounding in AI_OPPONENT.md §1 Area 2 (Stellaris insolvency -> handed alloys; the priority-and-score + spending-variables remedy). Forecast horizon: construction ticks_remaining + one clearing pass; the forecast reads only public market data (visibility-honest). Difficulty knobs (if any) are small transparent economic multipliers per §2 - never information or rule cheats.

items.title: AI skill-regression harness — seed-set bot-vs-bot goldens + tick-boundary state hash
items.summary: The data-strategy instrument (AI_OPPONENT.md §3): freeze a benchmark seed-set spanning body/terrain/market diversity; run headless bot-vs-bot rollouts; assert the AI holds its bands (solvency rate, net-worth curve, survival) as regression goldens - the AI analogue of verifier-headless, run on every AI change. Also lands the tick-boundary STATE HASH (a deterministic checksum over the econ-tick snapshot, the parked MULTIPLAYER_PRINCIPLES.md idea): today a two-runs-same-seed regression primitive for this harness, later the lockstep desync detector - one small addition serving both worlds. Authorise as a new verifier-headless check (tools/verify/ai_skill_harness.cpp) per the tool-creation-is-skill-creation rule.
items.design: Metrics per seed: per-corp net-worth curve (sampled every N ticks), solvency (ticks below zero balance), survival, action counts by verb (a thrash detector). Goldens are disposable per the golden culture - bless routinely, flag unexplained diffs. items.title: Corp blackboard export — dump the visibility-honest state export as versioned text facts

A headless flag --export-blackboard <corp|all> [--out <dir>] dumps each corp's §6 visibility-honest state export as JSONL facts — one per line {t(tick), subject, predicate, value, confidence, provenance} — deterministic ordering, schema version stamped per file. items.title: World history log — an append-only narrative substrate replacing the per-eval blackboard snapshot (enables a past-history game mode)
items.summary: Ben's pivot (2026-07-28), reacting to BL-206's snapshot-style blackboard export: re-deriving a fresh state summary from the world every time someone reads it is 'unnecessary and boring overhead.' Proposal: make the append-only EVENT LOG the source of truth from world generation onward, not a per-eval snapshot query. Concretely, the bones already exist and are scattered: corp_ai's decision ring (corp_decision_ring) is already an event log of AI commands; trade_routes (last_tick, convoy_count) is already history, not state; agency_event is already a live narrated feed; and PLANETOLOGY.md's per-body dated biography (S0-S9, already implemented under BL-167 - abiogenesis at S5 Spark, the oxygenation bottlenecks at S6 Breath, land colonisation at S7 Green) is already exactly 'how chemical life started and what evolution bottlenecks led to humans forming,' produced once at generation and never revisited. This item unifies those into one growing, replayable log spanning generation through simulation, with the corp_ai blackboard snapshot and the BL-206 JSONL export becoming a DERIVED VIEW over the log rather than an authored artifact. The payoff Ben named: a game can start reading the log from tick 0 instead of 'now,' which is most of what a 'play through the past' mode needs, close to free once the log is the substrate.
