2. **Derive the trait vector.** Each region gets a small fixed-width vector read off its own land and endowment - maritime vs riverine vs steppe vs highland origin, arable share, ore access, isolation, and (from BL-217) what there was to domesticate. Deterministic consequence, no dice.
3. **Grow nations over it.** Settlement and conflict history grows polities seeded from culture regions. A nation may hold several regions; a region may be cut across by a border. That mismatch is not a bug - it is the generated source of internal friction and irredentist claims, and it is exactly what a Voronoi partition cannot produce.
4. **Derive corporate focus from the result.** CORPORATION_GENERATION's authored focus table is replaced by the industrial character the settlement history actually produced. GENERATION_STRATEGY.md's economic premise - a saturated nation-owned substrate with lean specialist corporations - must survive this unchanged IN SPIRIT; it is the constraint the rewrite answers to, not a casualty of it.

## What culture feeds (all four accepted)

1. **Trade friction and affinity.** Cultural distance modifies route cost, market access, or counterparty willingness. This also gives BL-161's embargo / exclusive-trade lever a generated reason to exist rather than an arbitrary one.
2. **Demand preferences.** Culture shapes consumption baskets and endemic-good demand (BL-191), so two identically-endowed markets behave differently.
3. **Labour and industry character.** Workforce availability and productivity, and which industries a nation actually grew - feeding the substrate premise and corporate focus derivation.
4. **Conflict propensity.** Drives war and collapse branching DURING generation (BL-210's historical-extinction checkpoint), and nation-level friction at campaign start.

## Hidden, but its consequences are not - and that is the design

Ben: 'the player doesn't see this - it's just for the diplomacy and hidden AI layers.'

The trait vector is never surfaced. There is no culture lens, no culture entry in the Selection band, no name for a region in the UI. What the player sees is BEHAVIOUR: this market wants that good, this counterparty is difficult, this border is tense. The cause stays opaque; the effects are everywhere.

This is a deliberate and coherent position - it makes culture an explanation the world HAS and the player must infer, rather than a stat block to optimise against. State it explicitly in NATION_GENERATION.md when the work lands, because a future session will otherwise 'helpfully' add the lens.

**Developer inspection is SWEEP READOUT ONLY.** No Generation Ledger overlay. Culture appears as aggregate numbers in the batch output (BL-219) and nowhere else. Accepted risk, recorded here: a single nonsensical region will be hard to spot without a visual. If tuning proves that painful, a dev-only overlay is the escalation - not a player-facing one.

## Frozen at campaign start

Culture is a generation output and never moves during play. This respects the standing deferral on nation behaviour (backlog.json BL-054) and keeps the entire feature inside the generation layer, with zero runtime simulation. Drift from player action was offered and not taken.

## Determinism

- The clustering pass must be deterministic and order-independent - a tile's region assignment cannot depend on iteration order. Specify the tie-break explicitly.
- Fresh stage tags for the culture and settlement sub-streams.
- Trait vectors are fixed-point or integer. No floating-point comparison decides a region boundary.
- Region count and assignment must be identical across the determinism harness's twice-generated world (BL-106).

## Cut, by the diagnostic test

**Language families, religion, art, values, and named cultures** are all cut. None changes a decision - the four payoffs above are served entirely by the trait vector, and a hidden layer gains nothing from flavour it never shows. Note also the standing position that belief systems are Fable's territory, not this project's.

## Residual calls (doc-pass time)

1. Trait vector width and axes - the four payoffs constrain it, but the exact set is a doc-pass decision.
2. Whether the settlement/conflict history that grows nations is genuinely temporal (epochs, with BL-210's historical-extinction checkpoints firing) or a single scored pass. The checkpoint mechanism implies temporal; cost says check it.
3. How region-to-nation mismatch is represented in the data model, since it is the item's main structural payoff.
4. Whether Voronoi BFS is fully retired or retained as a fallback for bodies with no culture layer.

Read NATION_GENERATION.md and CORPORATION_GENERATION.md in full, GENERATION_STRATEGY.md's economic premise, and BL-210's settlement-stage sketch before promoting.

## UPDATE 2026-07-30

Step 1 of the mechanism above says region count is "a function of habitable land area and **its fragmentation**". **BL-221** (docs/lore/HISTORY.md Stages 0-2) is what generates fragmentation as a quantity: cradle count from arable/ocean/river connectivity, then conquest-cost and exit-cost scalars from the same terrain barriers this item clusters on. So the two interleave rather than stack - BL-221 produces the polity seeds and the fragmentation field, this item grows nations over them, and BL-221's Stage 2 line ("{n} realms confirm mutual borders") can only be written after that growth. Specify the interleave at doc-pass time.

Also: **BL-224** asserts the non-hegemony invariant in the harness (no nation holds more than X% of habitable land or of any strategic resource), which is the falsifiability this item's clustering currently lacks given its sweep-readout-only inspection call.

items.title: Whole-pipeline generation sweep - rarity targets, per-lean/per-branch cost, and the culture readout
items.summary: Rarity is sweep-tuned, not clamped - which makes the sweep load-bearing rather than a convenience. tools/verify/planetology_sweep.cpp samples seeds within the biosphere chain; this generalises it across the whole pipeline (continents -> biosphere -> evolution -> settlement -> culture) and adds the rarity bands BL-217's honest gates are tuned against. SETTLED 2026-07-29 (Ben, generation Q&A - three rounds, twelve calls). Sibling of BL-210, which named this stage but designed none of it.
items.design:
DESIGNED 2026-07-29 (Ben, Q&A). Filed as a separate sibling deliberately: folded into either BL-217 or BL-218 it would be the first thing cut under pressure, and it is the ONLY instrument that makes the 'tuned, not clamped' discipline actually enforceable.

## Why this is load-bearing now

Ben chose SWEEP-TUNED, NOT CLAMPED for how often the system's other bodies get life. That choice is only honest if the measurement exists. Without it 'rare' is a hope; the gates run, and nobody knows what they produce until a player complains that three moons grew forests.

The same argument covers BL-210's already-stated rule that no lean may be a dead end, now extended to branches - and BL-218's culture regions, which have NO visual inspector at all by Ben's call, making the sweep readout their only window.

## What it must measure

1. **Rarity bands.** Observed frequency across a seed sample of: any life, complex multicellular life, sapience, and completed-then-dead precursor civilisation - per body and per system. Ben's stated targets are qualitative (life rare, complexity very rare, sapience rarer still); the sweep's first job is turning those into numbers the constants can be tuned against.
2. **Per-lean and per-branch cost.** Today's sweep measures acceptance rate and per-lean cost within the biosphere chain. Extend to lean x branch-combination space across the whole pipeline, so a dead-end combination surfaces as a NUMBER rather than a bug report. This is BL-210's explicit ask: 'generate many worlds, to see what targets are best, and how to tweak the overall strategy.'
3. **Homeworld acceptance rate.** BL-217 adds five gates plus radiations the homeworld must clear, and BL-209 adds seven before that. Acceptance will fall and reject-and-reroll absorbs it - but per-lean cost must be re-measured so no preference becomes a dead end.
4. **Culture aggregate readout.** Region counts, trait-vector distributions, and region-to-nation mismatch rates. BL-218's only inspection surface.
5. **Generation time per stage.** Against Ben's 30s-per-stage ceiling. A stage that drifts past it should fail the sweep, not be discovered in a playtest.

## Reduced-fidelity mode

The 30s-per-stage ceiling and a thousand-seed batch are incompatible at full fidelity. The sweep needs a reduced-fidelity path that keeps every GATE and BRANCH decision exact while skipping expensive presentation-side work - the molecular event trace (BL-209), the narrative log entries (BL-208), and per-tile detail no gate reads.

**The invariant that makes this safe: reduced fidelity must produce IDENTICAL gate outcomes to a full run for the same seed.** That is itself an assertion the harness should carry - otherwise the tuning instrument and the shipped generator drift apart, and every number the sweep produces becomes a lie.

## Skill registration

Per CLAUDE.md 'Tool creation is skill creation', the extended sweep is registered in the verifier-headless skill so it is discoverable and re-runnable rather than a procedure someone remembers. It joins planetology_harness, chemistry_tables_harness, world_audit and world_determinism there.

## Residual calls (doc-pass time)

1. Sample size, and whether it is fixed or adaptive (run until the rarity estimate's confidence interval closes).
2. Output format - the existing sweep's table, or something diffable so a tuning change's effect is reviewable.
3. Whether rarity bands become hard harness assertions (R13 in BL-217) or advisory numbers. Assertions are stricter and will fail loudly during tuning, which is arguably the point.

Read tools/verify/planetology_sweep.cpp as it stands, PLANETOLOGY.md 'Verification' and 'The homeworld: preferences, a strict floor, and reject-and-reroll', and BL-210's batch-tuning section before promoting.

## UPDATE 2026-07-30 - two more things to measure

The docs/lore/HISTORY.md ladder (BL-221/222/223) extends the pipeline again, and Ben's framing for it is a direct instruction to this item:

> "For now, we want data on what kinds of worlds are interesting, so it would actually be valuable to see many failure cases, and find out what parameters should be tweaked for interesting gameplay." (Ben, 2026-07-30)

So failure cases are **wanted output**, and this sweep is where they are counted rather than hidden. Two additions:

6. **Historical-ladder outcomes.** Distribution of cradle count, fragmentation, nation count, first-industrialiser identity, industrialisation date and per-nation drawdown across a seed sample - the numbers BL-221/222's constants get tuned against.
7. **Hegemony rate.** BL-224's N1-N5 are measured as a RATE across seeds, not enforced per world (constrain the inputs, never the gates). The build fails when the rate exceeds its threshold; an individual hegemon world is a data point, not a rejection.

Also pin the **nation-count band** here by measurement: HISTORY.md asserts ~45 nations, the build generates 14. BL-224's N1 cannot be written until this sweep says what the generator actually does.

items.title: history_event cannot date a year - a historical-epoch timestamp for the oral history log
items.summary: FOUNDATION for the HISTORY.md ladder (BL-221/222/223) and cheap enough to land alone. history_event (planetology.hpp:121) timestamps with `float gya` - billions of years before present. Every stage of the historical ladder is dated in YEARS ("-XXXX: First granary cities", "YYYY: The {nation} Charter Act"); 1450 CE is 5.1e-7 Gya, which will not sort, print, or survive tuning at float precision. Land the timestamp change before any historical stage emits a line, not during.
items.design:
DESIGNED 2026-07-30 (from the docs/lore/HISTORY.md review). Filed separately and first because four items (BL-209, BL-211, BL-217, and the three HISTORY.md ladder items) all append to the same `history_event` stream, and discovering the timestamp problem mid-item means reworking every one of them.

## The defect

`src/world/planetology.hpp:121`:

```
struct history_event {
    float       gya = 0.0f;   ///< Billions of years before present.
    chain_stage stage = chain_stage::system;
    std::string event;
    std::string consequence;
};
```

`gya` is correct and legible for the deep-time chain it was built for - S0 accretion at 4.5, the GOE at 2.4, land colonisation at 0.5. It cannot express a historical date at all:

- 1450 CE is 5.1e-7 Gya. At `float` precision the whole of recorded history collapses into the last few representable steps before zero, so two events centuries apart can compare equal.
- The ledger prints `4.5 Gya` / `now`. There is no format that reads sensibly for both 4.5 Gya and 1687 CE from one field.
- Sorting is the real hazard: the biography is a single ordered list, and the historical stages interleave into the same list as the deep-time ones.

## The shape

One timestamp field that spans both regimes, not two parallel fields the consumers must branch on. Recommended: a **signed integer year relative to the campaign epoch** (1 Jan 1960, ERAS.md), wide enough for 4.5 Gyr - `int64_t years_before_epoch`, or a fixed-point pair if the harness prefers it. Deep-time lines carry a round number of years; historical lines carry an exact one. `gya` becomes a derived accessor for display, not storage.

Why an integer and not a double: PLANETOLOGY.md § Determinism & cost already bans implementation-defined float behaviour from gate paths, and a timestamp that participates in sorting is effectively a gate path. Integer years sort exactly, tie-break deterministically, and serialise without a format decision.

## Display, which is the actual user-visible half

The existing ledger (`tile_inspector.cpp`, the "Generation History" section shipped in b90ba10) formats a dated two-column line. It needs a formatter that picks the unit from the magnitude, on PLANETOLOGY.md § Presentation's "do not linearise deep time" rule:

| Magnitude | Reads as |
|---|---|
| > 1 Myr | `4.5 Gya`, `252 Mya` |
| 1 kyr - 1 Myr | `11,650 years ago` |
| within recorded history | `1687`, `-3200` |
| 0 | `now` |

This is a presentation rule, not a data one - the same field drives all four.

## Migration

Every current emitter writes `gya` directly (`planetology.cpp`, `continents.cpp`). The change is mechanical and the harness pins it: `planetology_harness` R1 (determinism) and R2 (four bodies land in their archetypes) both compare history contents, so a botched conversion fails loudly.

## Residual calls (doc-pass time)

1. `int64_t` years vs a fixed-point pair - decide against how the eventual serialiser wants it (no serialiser exists today; PLANETOLOGY.md § Determinism & cost notes bodies are few and inline-on-body_component is right).
2. Whether `chain_stage` gains the historical stages (BL-221/222/223 add them) or the historical ladder carries its own parallel enum. Prefer one enum - a single ordered biography is the whole presentation model.

Read PLANETOLOGY.md § Presentation and § Determinism & cost, and the "Generation History" section in src/ui/tile_inspector.cpp, before promoting.

items.title: The pre-national history ladder - agrarian surplus, the enforceable promise, and fragmentation-with-connectivity (HISTORY.md Stages 0-2)
items.summary: The first half of the stage ladder in docs/lore/HISTORY.md (new, from Fable): Stage 0 agrarian surplus, Stage 1 the enforceable promise / Charter Age, Stage 2 fragmentation-with-connectivity. Fills the first part of the stage BL-210 named but designed none of ("Settlement -> Industrialisation -> 1900s"). SETTLED 2026-07-30 (Ben): the ladder is 100% DRIVEN, not narrated - Stage 0 cradle count drives fragmentation, which drives the region count and nation count BL-218 forms polities over. Sibling of BL-222 (Stages 3-4) and BL-223 (Stages 5-6).
items.design:
DESIGNED 2026-07-30 (Ben, HISTORY.md review). The load-bearing call: **the ladder DRIVES, it does not narrate.**

> "100% driven. We are escaping the previous view where input -> output is exactly determined. For now, we want data on what kinds of worlds are interesting, so it would actually be valuable to see many failure cases, and find out what parameters should be tweaked for interesting gameplay." (Ben, 2026-07-30)

Read as: the knob-to-outcome map stops being closed-form, because outcomes now emerge from stages interacting. **Determinism is untouched** - the pass stays a pure function of (campaign_seed, ...), per the standing rule and PLANETOLOGY.md § Determinism & cost. *Flagged for confirmation at doc-pass time: if Ben meant something stronger than "not closed-form", that is a standing-rule change and must be raised explicitly, not assumed here.*

The second half of that quote is a scope instruction as much as a tuning one: **failure cases are wanted output, not defects.** The ladder is never rejected for producing a fragmented, poor, or late-industrialising world. That is BL-219's measurement surface, and the reason rarity is sweep-tuned rather than clamped.

## Where this sits

BL-210 sketched `Settlement -> Industrialisation -> 1900s` and explicitly deferred its design. `docs/lore/HISTORY.md` is that design, arriving as a causal ladder rather than a single pass. It splits three ways by what each half drives:

| Item | Stages | Drives |
|---|---|---|
| **BL-221 (this)** | 0 Surplus, 1 Charter, 2 Fragmentation | region count / nation count / fragmentation (feeds BL-218) |
| BL-222 | 3 Capital, 4 Energy | S9 drawdown, first-industrialiser, industrial character |
| BL-223 | 5 Rupture, 6 Saturation | the campaign premise itself |

Stages 0-2 must run **before** BL-218 forms nations, because BL-218 already states its region count is "a function of habitable land area and its fragmentation" - and this ladder is what generates fragmentation as a quantity rather than an adjective.

## The three stages

**Stage 0 - Agrarian surplus.** Surplus food -> dense settlements -> division of labour -> strangers who must trade rather than share. Reads arable share, ocean fraction and river connectivity (BL-170) off the tile map and BL-217's domesticable-clade output. Emits a **cradle count**: how many independent agricultural origins the land supports, and where. HISTORY.md: "More cradles -> deeper eventual fragmentation (feeds Stage 2)."

Line: `"-XXXX: First granary cities on the {region} floodplain."`

**Stage 1 - The enforceable promise / the Charter Age.** Contract law extends past kinship: partnership, credit, then the charter - an entity that outlives its members and can own, sue, and be sued. HISTORY.md is correct that the game's own rule already IS this doctrine made mechanical: *"A corporation persists as long as it holds at least one asset"* (GLOSSARY.md, CONCEPT.md:7). No new mechanic is needed; the stage generates its **origin**.

The Kepler divergence HISTORY.md asks for is that the charter arrives EARLY relative to Earth, and that it is registered-in-a-home-nation-but-operationally-free - which is exactly the bargain CORPORATION_GENERATION.md already describes (taxable and seizable in exchange for freedom of operation). What this stage drives: which nation's legal tradition the charter came from, and how early - feeding corporate focus derivation in BL-218 step 4.

Line: `"YYYY: The {nation} Charter Act - first perpetual company registered."`

**Stage 2 - Fragmentation with connectivity.** Many competing states, close enough to trade, copy and poach; none able to conquer the rest. HISTORY.md's causal claim is the one worth keeping verbatim: *"A hegemon can CHOOSE stagnation - suppress a technology by decree and it stays suppressed. Forty-five rivals cannot: a capability banned in one polity re-emerges next door. Competition among states is the market mechanism applied to governance itself."*

The generator hook is the terrain barriers BL-218 already clusters on - mountain ranges, deserts, open water, absent arable land - now consumed a second time to decide how EXPENSIVE conquest is and how CHEAP exit is. Output: a fragmentation scalar plus the polity-seed count BL-218 grows nations from.

Line: `"YYYY: The {range} Peace - {n} realms confirm mutual borders."`

## What it drives (the whole point of "100% driven")

1. **Cradle count -> fragmentation -> region and nation count.** Today `nation_generation.cpp` seeds Voronoi arbitrarily and merges anything under `min_nation_tiles` (80). Under BL-218 the seeds come from culture regions; under this item the NUMBER of them is a historical outcome.
2. **Conquest cost / exit cost.** A single scalar pair from Stage 2's barrier read, consumed by BL-218's settlement-and-conflict growth and by BL-224's non-hegemony assertion.
3. **The charter's home tradition and date**, feeding corporate focus derivation.

## Presentation

Three lines into the existing biography, in the ledger shipped by b90ba10 (nav slot 9, "Generation History"). Every line carries its consequence in the right column - PLANETOLOGY.md § Presentation, non-negotiable. No codex, no separate surface: HISTORY.md's own open question 3 ("codex, generated lines, or ambient flavour?") is answered by the surface already existing.

Entries are authored into BL-208's append-only world log, not a parallel structure - same call BL-217 made, same reason.

## Determinism

Fresh stage tags per stage; per-stage hashed sub-streams (PLANETOLOGY.md warns 0x4A71012u is already folded twice in hard_coded_world.cpp). Cradle scoring and barrier costs are integer or fixed-point with an explicit tie-break by tile index - a float argmax over regions is a portability hazard and a tie-break nightmare, the same objection BL-218 raises for its trait vectors. No bare transcendentals in any gate path.

## Cut, by the diagnostic test

PLANETOLOGY.md: "for every generated value, name the decision it changes. Anything that fails is deleted, not tuned." Provisionally cut: **named historical polities and rulers** (worldbuilding, changes nothing); **a coinage/currency stage** (HISTORY.md itself argues the deep enabler is the enforceable promise, not coinage - so coinage is a line at most, never a gate); **writing/literacy as its own gate** (real, invisible downstream).

## Residual calls (doc-pass time)

1. Whether Stage 0-2 are three gates with failure states (a world with too few cradles never fragments, and gets a hegemon - which BL-224 then has to assert against) or three scored passes with no failure. Ben wants failure cases visible, which argues for gates.
2. Whether the fragmentation scalar is one number or a per-region field. Per-region is truer and is what BL-218's clustering would rather consume.
3. Ordering against BL-218 in detail: this item produces seeds, BL-218 grows polities, and Stage 2's "n realms confirm mutual borders" line can only be written AFTER growth. So the ladder interleaves with BL-218 rather than strictly preceding it - specify the interleave.
4. Whether the ~45 nations HISTORY.md asserts is a target for this stage or an emergent number. Today's build generates 14 (BL-094 references "the 14 generated Voronoi nations"), so the gap is 3x and someone must own it.

Read docs/lore/HISTORY.md in full, BL-218's mechanism section, BL-210's settlement-stage sketch, and NATION_GENERATION.md before promoting.

items.title: The industrial history ladder - capital disciplines the sovereign, and the energy transition (HISTORY.md Stages 3-4)
items.summary: The second half of the docs/lore/HISTORY.md ladder: Stage 3 capital disciplines the sovereign (states become credit-dependent and therefore commitment-bound), Stage 4 the energy transition (fossil fuels break the organic ceiling; each seed gets its own Britain). Drives the S9 drawdown scalar - which is what makes PLANETOLOGY.md S9's stated inversion ("a richer endowment industrialises EARLIER and is therefore MORE drawn down at campaign start") a generated quantity instead of one authored constant. Also the mechanism the post-WW2 industrial grounding open item in GENERATION_STRATEGY.md has been waiting for.
items.design:
DESIGNED 2026-07-30 (Ben, HISTORY.md review). Sibling of BL-221; same "100% driven, failure cases wanted" call applies (see BL-221 for the quote and the determinism reading).

## Stage 3 - Capital disciplines the sovereign

Interstate competition (BL-221 Stage 2) makes states dependent on credit, therefore on merchants and bond markets, therefore forced into credible commitment. States that default or confiscate lose the next war.

HISTORY.md's lesson is the one that matters for the campaign premise: *"this is why the campaign's nations respect corporate property in 1960: their ancestors that didn't were outcompeted."* Without this stage, "nations tolerate corporations" is an assertion. With it, it is a generated outcome with named losers.

**What it drives:** a per-nation *commitment* / creditworthiness character, which feeds nation political character (today assigned by NATION_GENERATION.md's own pass) and the corporate operating freedom in CORPORATION_GENERATION.md. A nation that confiscated its way through this stage is one whose charters are worth less - a generated reason for the industrial-focus spread rather than an authored table.

**Its runtime echo is deliberately NOT in this item.** HISTORY.md asks that asset seizure carry a sentiment/credit cost consistent with this stage; nothing in `src/` implements seizure at all, and nation behaviour is deferred by standing rule. Filed separately as **BL-225**, parked behind Laws/Politics.

## Stage 4 - Energy transition

Fossil fuels break the organic-economy ceiling; growth compounds; wealth stops being zero-sum land. HISTORY.md: *"Coal-near-cities made Britain - endowment, not virtue. Once wealth compounds, conquest's return-on-investment collapses relative to trade's, which changes what war is FOR."*

This is the stage most sensitive to the endowment vector, and the cheapest to implement honestly, because the data already exists. PLANETOLOGY.md S8 already generates coal rank (only mid-bituminous cokes), petroleum, and the iron endowment with its oxic-weathering grade upgrade; nation resource profiles are already derived by summing tile deposits. So the pass can **name which nation industrialised first purely from tile data** - fossil accessibility and ore grade on owned tiles, against BL-221's bulk-transport and river connectivity (BL-170). *Each seed gets its own Britain.*

Keep PLANETOLOGY.md S8's counterweight visible: charcoal reduced iron at industrial scale for two millennia, so **coke gates cheap steel, not steel**. A coal-rich but non-coking world industrialises late and expensively rather than not at all - which is a far more interesting outcome than a binary, and is exactly the kind of failure case Ben asked to see more of.

Line: `"YYYY: {nation} lights the first coke furnaces of the {region} basin."`

## The payoff: S9 drawdown becomes generated

PLANETOLOGY.md S9 today takes `drawdown` as a player preference (0-0.95) and asserts the inversion - richer endowment industrialises earlier, therefore is more drawn down at campaign start. BL-217 already promised to make industrialisation TIMING a generated quantity from the winning body plan's traits. This stage closes the loop: **timing x endowment -> drawdown**, per nation and per resource, instead of one global scalar.

That is what turns Era 0 -> Era 1 into a *pressure* rather than a menu choice, which GENERATION_STRATEGY.md's economic premise asserts but does not currently generate.

Note the interaction to specify, not discover: the `drawdown` preference must become a **lean** biasing this outcome, not a value competing with it - the same reconciliation PLANETOLOGY.md § Open calls 5 demands for `deposit_scalar` vs the endowment vector. Two independent levers multiplying makes both uninterpretable.

## The post-WW2 grounding item, finally answered

GENERATION_STRATEGY.md and CORPORATION_GENERATION.md both carry an unsettled note: *"the focus->asset-mix patterns should be grounded in research on the post-WW2 industries that led to space-related capability, so a specialist's holdings read as a plausible pathway toward off-world reach rather than an arbitrary mix."* Stage 4's output IS that grounding - an industrial character derived from which fuels and ores a nation actually had, in which order. Close that open item as part of landing this one, or explicitly state why it stays open.

## Determinism

As BL-221. Fresh stage tags; integer/fixed-point scoring for the first-industrialiser argmax with an explicit tie-break by nation id; the rank and grade curves already exist as binned lookups from BL-167 and must be reused, not re-derived with transcendentals.

## Harness impact

`planetology_harness` gains assertions that (a) the first-industrialiser is a deterministic function of tile fossil/ore data, not of iteration order over `world.bodies` (an `unordered_map` - the sorted-walk rule in PLANETOLOGY.md § Determinism applies); (b) a coal-rich non-coking world still industrialises, late; (c) drawdown correlates with industrialisation date in the stated direction, across a seed spread. (c) belongs to BL-219's sweep if it is expensive.

## Residual calls (doc-pass time)

1. Per-nation vs global drawdown. Per-nation is truer and is what the "which nation industrialised first" line implies, but the economy today reads one body-level endowment - check the cost before committing.
2. Whether Stage 3's commitment character replaces NATION_GENERATION.md's existing political-character assignment or feeds it.
3. How much of the depletion constants stay free parameters. PLANETOLOGY.md § Known weaknesses is blunt that "the depletion inversion is a design assertion dressed as a finding" - do not let this item quietly promote it to physics.

Read docs/lore/HISTORY.md Stages 3-4, PLANETOLOGY.md S8/S9 and § Known weaknesses, GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § Open cross-doc items, and BL-221 before promoting.

items.title: The averted rupture - a Cold War that did not go hot as the origin of diplomacy, and the premise reframed for the nation-with-chartered-corps identity
items.summary: HISTORY.md Stages 5-6 as delivered by Fable assume a WW3-scale global rupture that already happened, and frame the whole ladder as answering "why is the player a corporation". Ben rejected both halves 2026-07-30: the near-catastrophe was AVERTED (a Cold War that did not go hot), and it is the origin of DIPLOMACY as a system; and the player identity is a nation with chartered corps (BL-094), so the thesis needs re-pointing. Three docs currently disagree on where the rupture sits - CONCEPT.md:51 puts it at Era 0's exit, ERAS.md's Era 0->1 gate is purely mechanical, HISTORY.md puts it in the past. DESIGN-OWED because the reframe changes the ladder's payoff stage, not just its wording.
items.design:
DESIGN-OWED, opened 2026-07-30 from the docs/lore/HISTORY.md review. Two of Ben's answers landed here and both invalidate what the doc currently says.

## What HISTORY.md says today

**Stage 5 - The Rupture.** *"The WW3-scale global rupture that closes Era 0's backstory. Every claimant to hegemony fights; every one is exhausted, winners included."* Its framing rule is load-bearing by its own account: the event should discredit territorial conquest, leave corporations as the only actors with intact cross-border capacity, and create a deterrence ceiling forcing ambition into economic channels - *"that single framing answers, in one stroke: why the player is a corporation, why nations tolerate it, and why rivals compete through markets rather than armies."*

**Stage 6 - Saturation, 1960.** The saturated background economy is the *post-hegemonic condition*, not a neutral start. Expansion happens from saturation, not strength.

## Ben's two corrections (2026-07-30)

> "I think the backlog holds too many conflicting ideas, so my intent was a bit lost. I don't know precisely what you mean by Rupture, but the idea is that the player is a nation with chartered corps, no longer just a corporation. If the docs don't reflect that, please update. Specifically, cold war can be one example of an Era 0 which was averted, and we will use it as an example which caused diplomacy to really evolve and begin."

**(a) The catastrophe was AVERTED, not survived.** Not a WW3 that happened and exhausted everyone - a rupture that came close and did not fire. The 1960 epoch (ERAS.md) is already literally the Cold War, so this needs no invention: the world of 1960 is one that looked over the edge.

**(b) Its payoff is DIPLOMACY, not corporate primacy.** The averted catastrophe is what "caused diplomacy to really evolve and begin". This is a better fit for what the build actually has than the original framing was - BL-212 (nation-voiced public comms) shipped, BL-205 (channel-based corp chat log, diplomacy as communication) is designed at A/v0.2.0, and neither had a generated origin story. Now they do.

**(c) The identity is nation-with-chartered-corps.** This is already settled and already documented - **BL-094** (designed, parked F, v0.2.0): the player pivots to the nation as strategic actor owning research/military/intelligence, with the chartered corp as the economic actor, prototyped as one. ROADMAP § v0.2.0 carries it. So the docs DO reflect it; what does not is `docs/lore/HISTORY.md`, which was written against the older single-corporation identity, and `CONCEPT.md:4` which still reads *"corporate or nation-state entity. The exact form is undecided"* - a line BL-094 owns and which must not be edited ahead of the v0.2.0 cut (standing rule: authority docs propagate as part of landing the work).

**The reframe is a strict improvement, not a loss.** Stage 1's Charter Age is *already* about the sovereign-and-chartered-company bargain. Under the corporate identity the ladder answered "why is the player a corporation"; under the nation identity it answers **"why does a nation act through chartered corporations, and why does it tolerate their cross-border operation"** - which is the same causal chain aimed at a question the game actually asks.

## The three-doc disagreement to settle

| Doc | Says |
|---|---|
| `CONCEPT.md:51` | Era 0's *exit* "is not a quiet graduation; a 'WW3'-scale global rupture reshapes the world enough that a rapid space expansion becomes plausible" - a FUTURE event, during play |
| `ERAS.md` § Era 0 -> Era 1 gate | Three purely mechanical conditions (Rocketry research, Launchpad staffed, propellant reserve). No event at all |
| `docs/lore/HISTORY.md` Stage 5 | A PAST event, backstory closing Era 0 |

All three cannot stand. The averted-rupture reading resolves it cleanly and is the direction this item takes: **the near-miss is in the past** (it is why 1960 is multipolar, diplomatic, and corporate-tolerant), and **Era 0's exit stays mechanical**. Whether the exit ALSO carries a narrative beat is a separate, smaller call.

## What the doc pass owes

1. **Rewrite HISTORY.md Stages 5-6** for the averted rupture and the diplomacy payoff, and re-point § Purpose claim 3 and § The compact thesis at the nation-with-chartered-corps identity.
2. **Settle the CONCEPT.md:51 conflict.** Either amend it (it is not BL-094-owned text) or state why the future-rupture reading survives alongside the past near-miss.
3. **Decide seeded vs canonical** - HISTORY.md's own open question 1. Seeded (which nations nearly fought, over what, and what pulled them back) is consistent with the rest of the generation stack and with Ben's "100% driven" call on BL-221; canonical is cheaper to write quest and tech fiction against. Recommend seeded, with the *shape* canonical: every campaign has an averted rupture, the belligerents and the trigger vary.
4. **Decide the deterrence ceiling** - HISTORY.md open question 2. Does Kepler get an explicit nuclear-equivalent, or is the memory of the near-miss the whole ceiling? This is the one call here that reaches forward into Era 1+ conflict design (BL-157), so it is worth answering deliberately rather than by default.
5. **State what Stage 5 drives**, since BL-221/222 are both driven and this stage must be too. Candidates: the diplomatic posture each nation opens with; the conflict-propensity input BL-218 lists as payoff 4; the deterrence constraint that keeps Era 0 conflict economic. Anything that drives nothing is deleted, not tuned (PLANETOLOGY.md § Presentation).
6. **Stage 6 mostly already exists** - GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § economic premise (saturated substrate, lean specialists, live opportunity gap) and PLANETOLOGY.md S9 (drawdown) are Stage 6. The owed work is one causal sentence connecting them to the averted rupture, plus confirming BL-222's generated drawdown supersedes S9's authored scalar.

## Why this is design-owed rather than designed

BL-221 and BL-222 can be promoted on the strength of HISTORY.md as written. Stages 5-6 cannot: the doc's version is a WW3 that happened, aimed at a player identity the project has since moved past. That is a design conversation, not a wording pass - and per Ben's own note ("the backlog holds too many conflicting ideas, so my intent was a bit lost"), the value here is in *removing* a conflicting idea rather than adding one.

Read docs/lore/HISTORY.md Stages 5-6 and § Open questions, CONCEPT.md § Eras, ERAS.md § Era 0 -> Era 1 gate, BL-094 in full, and BL-205/BL-212 for what diplomacy currently is, before designing.

items.title: Non-hegemony as an asserted generation invariant - no seed may produce a world-conquering nation
items.summary: The campaign premise makes three historical claims (docs/lore/HISTORY.md § Purpose); claim 2 - "~45 nations coexist; none can conquer the rest" - is the only one nothing checks. HISTORY.md calls Stage 2 non-hegemony "the single cheapest lore assertion with the largest downstream payoff". SETTLED 2026-07-30 (Ben): ASSERTED IN THE HARNESS, not left as narrative. A seed that hands one nation 60% of the habitable land silently falsifies the premise, and today nobody would find out until a playtest.
items.design:
DESIGNED 2026-07-30 (Ben, HISTORY.md review - "Asserted in the harness"). Per CLAUDE.md § Tool creation is skill creation, the check is authored as a harness assertion and registered in the `verifier-headless` skill, not run as a one-off.

## What is being asserted

HISTORY.md § Purpose claim 2 and Stage 2. The reasoning is worth keeping because it is what makes the assertion load-bearing rather than decorative: *"A hegemon can CHOOSE stagnation - suppress a technology by decree and it stays suppressed. Forty-five rivals cannot: a capability banned in one polity re-emerges next door."* Non-hegemony is not flavour; it is the precondition for markets, dynamic prices, and cross-border corporate operation - i.e. for the game.

## The assertions

Candidate set, thresholds to be pinned by measurement (BL-219) rather than chosen here:

| # | Assertion | Reads |
|---|---|---|
| N1 | Nation count sits inside a stated band | `nation_generation` output |
| N2 | No single nation holds more than X% of habitable land | owner_map + habitability |
| N3 | No single nation holds more than X% of any Era 0 strategic resource's accessible deposits | owner_map + deposits |
| N4 | Terrain barriers actually land on borders at better than chance | owner_map + terrain landform |
| N5 | The largest nation cannot cheaply reach the smallest - conquest cost above a floor | BL-221 Stage 2's conquest/exit scalars + BL-146 road/A* cost |

N2 is the minimum viable version and is worth landing alone if the rest slip. N3 matters more for the *economy* than N2 does - a nation with a monopoly on accessible coal breaks the market premise without holding much land. N4 is what makes BL-218's clustering falsifiable rather than merely plausible.

## The nation-count gap someone must own

HISTORY.md asserts **~45 nations**. The build generates **14** (BL-094: "the player IS one of the 14 generated Voronoi nations"), with `min_nation_tiles = 80` merging anything smaller (`nation_generation.hpp:51`). That is a 3x gap, and N1 cannot be written until it is settled: either HISTORY.md's number is aspirational and the band is 12-20, or the grid and merge threshold change. **Flag, do not silently pick** - a harness that asserts 45 against a generator that makes 14 is a red build, and one that asserts 14 quietly retires a premise claim.

## Failure is a report, not a reroll

Ben's BL-221 call - *"it would actually be valuable to see many failure cases"* - applies here. A seed that produces a hegemon should be **reported by the sweep**, not rejected by the generator. The harness assertion runs over a fixed seed set and fails the build if the RATE exceeds a threshold; it does not gate individual world generation. This is PLANETOLOGY.md's own discipline (constrain the inputs, never the gates) and BL-217's "sweep-tuned, not clamped".

That split is the important design point here, and it should be stated in the harness comments: **N1-N5 are tuning targets measured across seeds, not per-world preconditions.**

## Where it lives

`tools/verify/world_audit.cpp` already walks the generated world and already carries threshold assertions (its S2 forest+wetland balance threshold caught BL-210's continent bias being 3x too strong). N1-N4 are natural additions. The per-seed RATE aggregation belongs in `planetology_sweep.cpp` under BL-219, which is already extending to whole-pipeline measurement.

## Residual calls (doc-pass time)

1. The nation-count band (see above). Blocking for N1 only.
2. Thresholds for N2/N3 - measure first, per Ben's standing "measure before reshaping".
3. Whether N5 is affordable, given it needs BL-221's conquest-cost scalars and an A* pass. Cut it first if not.
4. Whether a hegemon world gets a named archetype the way a dead body does. A "Hegemony" outcome that the sweep counts is more useful than an assertion failure with no name.

Read docs/lore/HISTORY.md § Purpose and Stage 2, tools/verify/world_audit.cpp as it stands, BL-219, and NATION_GENERATION.md before promoting.

items.title: Asset seizure costs the seizing nation - sentiment and credit access, not a free confiscation
items.summary: The one runtime mechanic docs/lore/HISTORY.md asks for: Stage 3 ("capital disciplines the sovereign") argues nations respect corporate property in 1960 because their ancestors that confiscated were outcompeted - so seizure must exist and must COST the seizer in sentiment and credit access. Progressive loss rather than a lose screen, mirroring the historical norm that sovereigns squeezed companies far more often than they destroyed them. Seizure is named as a loss vector in CONCEPT.md:41 and CORPORATION_GENERATION.md:21 but exists NOWHERE in src/. FILED 2026-07-30 (Ben: "file it, parked for Laws/Politics") so the claim is not lost; parked because nation behaviour is deferred by standing rule.
items.design:
DESIGN-OWED, filed 2026-07-30 from the docs/lore/HISTORY.md review. Parked deliberately - this is recorded so the ladder's single runtime claim survives, not queued.

## The claim

HISTORY.md Stage 3, § Game-mechanical echo: *"Asset seizure exists but is costly to the seizing nation (sentiment, credit access). Progressive loss instead of a lose screen mirrors the historical norm: sovereigns squeezed companies far more often than they destroyed them."*

This is the mechanical consequence of the stage's lesson - if confiscation were free, the generated history that produced commitment-bound sovereigns would be contradicted by the runtime every time a nation seized something.

## Current state of the build

- `CONCEPT.md:41` - *"Losing ground, going bankrupt, or having assets seized are impactful and progressive forms of defeat"*, and § Bankruptcy and seizure names financial collapse and military takeover as the two loss vectors.
- `CORPORATION_GENERATION.md:21` - a home nation may *"seize the corporation's domestic assets"*.
- `src/` - **nothing.** No seizure, no sentiment, no credit access, no nation-initiated action of any kind on player assets. Nation behaviour beyond the data-model minimum is prohibited by standing rule; the only sanctioned exceptions are BL-079's narrow per-building corp agency and BL-181's workforce dial.

So this is not a gap in an existing mechanic; it is a mechanic that does not exist yet, with a design constraint attached in advance.

## Why parked, and what it waits on

| Requires | Why |
|---|---|
| **BL-155** Laws & policy surface (design-owed, v0.1.2) | seizure is a policy act and needs a law surface to be taken from |
| **BL-158** Politics data-model stub (design-owed, v0.1.5) | sentiment has to live somewhere |
| **BL-094** nation-as-strategic-actor (designed, parked, v0.2.0) | under the nation identity the player can be the SEIZER as well as the seized, which is the whole reason the cost matters - a cost only ever paid by AI nations is invisible |

BL-094 is the important one. A seizure mechanic designed while the player is purely a corporation is a mechanic the player only ever suffers. Designed after the pivot, it is a lever with a price - which is what Stage 3 is actually about.

## What the design pass owes

1. What sentiment IS - whose opinion, tracked at what grain (nation-to-nation, nation-to-corp, market-level), and what it changes. Anything it does not change is deleted, not tuned.
2. What "credit access" means against the existing budget system (`src/world/budget_system.*`) - a rate, a ceiling, or a refusal.
3. Whether the cost is symmetrical (standing rule: symmetrical rules, and under BL-094 the player is the same kind of entity as its rivals).
4. Whether BL-222 Stage 3's generated per-nation commitment character sets each nation's STARTING sentiment and credit standing - it should, or the generated history hands nothing to the runtime and the stage is decorative.

Do not promote ahead of BL-155 and BL-158. Read docs/lore/HISTORY.md Stage 3, CONCEPT.md § Bankruptcy and seizure, and BL-094 before designing.
